Russians and British were allies against Napoleon, and enemies in the Crimean War of the 1850s, and rivals in the Great Game for control of central Asia in the late 19th century. were allies again in World Wars I and II, relations strained by Russian Revolution of 1917. were at sword's point during the Cold War (1947–91). Russian big businesses had strong connections with the City of London and British corporations during the late 1990s and 2000s.
 Nicholas II of Russia: Nicholas II or Nikolai II (Russian: Николай II Алекса́ндрович , "Nikolay II Aleksandrovich" ; 18 May [O.S. 6 May] 1868 – 17 July 1918) was last Emperor of Russia, ruling from 1 November 1894 until his forced abdication on 15 March 1917. His reign saw fall of Russian Empire from being one of foremost great powers of world to economic and military collapse.Due to Khodynka Tragedy, anti-Semitic pogroms, Bloody Sunday, violent suppression of 1905 Revolution, execution of political opponents and his perceived responsibility for Russo-Japanese War, he was given nickname Nicholas the Bloody by his political adversaries. Soviet historiography portrayed Nicholas as a weak and incompetent leader, whose decisions led to military defeats and deaths of millions of his subjects.
 Charles Sydney Gibbes: Charles Sydney Gibbes (19 January 1876 – 24 March 1963) was a British academic who from 1908 to 1917 served as English tutor to children of Emperor Nicholas II of Russia. When Nicholas abdicated throne in March 1917 Gibbes voluntarily accompanied Imperial family into exile to Siberian village of Tobolsk. After family was murdered in 1918 Gibbes returned to the United Kingdom became an Orthodox monk, adopting name of "Nicholas" in commemoration of Nicholas II. He died in 1963, buried at Headington cemetery, Oxford, Oxfordshire, England.
 Prince Andrew Romanov: Prince Andrew Andreyevich Romanov (born 21 January 1923) is a Russian American artist and author. He is a grand-nephew of Russia's last Emperor, Nicholas II. Since December 31, 2016 he is a claimant to headship of Imperial House of Russia and President of Romanov Family Association. He is a great-great-grandson in male-line of Emperor Nicholas I of Russia.

Castle Air Force Base: Castle Air Force Base (1941–1995) is a former United States Air Force Strategic Air Command base located northeast of Atwater, northwest of Merced about 115 miles (185 km) south of Sacramento, California.
 Sierra Academy of Aeronautics: The Sierra Academy of Aeronautics is an aviation flight school headquartered in Atwater, California It operates its training facility at former Castle Air Force Base in Atwater, California. Sierra Academy is also contracted by several foreign air carriers to perform pilot training, including Shanghai Airlines.
 ATP Flight School: ATP Flight School, headquartered in Jacksonville, Florida, is the largest flight training company in United States. privately held company founded in Atlanta, GA by current management, a small group of airline pilots, in 1984. ATP’s initial focus was providing flight training to U.S. military pilots seeking Airline Transport Pilot Certificates to transition over to commercial air carrier operations. Maintaining focus on professional flight training, ATP later expanded course offerings to include ab-initio training programs for domestic and international students, seeking career in commercial aviation. Today, ATP is the leading supplier of professionally trained pilots to nation's regional airlines.
 American Flyers (flight school): American Flyers is an American flight school. It the oldest flight training school in United States, founded at Midway Airport in 1939 by Reed Pigman. In 1980 flight school chain Aviation Training Enterprises, A.T.E, acquired American Flyers. company operates a chain of facilities at airports all across United States. American Flyers produces more instrument-rated pilots than any other school in nation. Previously based in West Chicago, Illinois, in building now taken over by Avel Flight School, American Flyers has nine locations across United States providing flight training to domestic and international students. An FAA-approved part 141 school, American Flyers offers a 6 months program uses rigid training course syllabus and standardized instructors.
Jeremiah Atwater: Jeremiah Atwater (December 27, 1773 – July 29, 1858) was notable as educator, minister, college president. Atwater became principal of Addison County Grammar School in 1799, a year later, when school became Middlebury College, assumed role of its first president. In 1809 Atwater left Middlebury to become third president of Dickinson College in Pennsylvania. remained in position until 1815, returned to New Haven, Connecticut, his birthplace and home of his alma mater, Yale University. Atwater Commons, one of five residential commons at Middlebury, is named for him. Dickinson College also has Atwater Hall named for him. Atwater was elected a member of the American Antiquarian Society in 1815.

Baraki Barak: Baraki Barak is a town and center of Baraki Barak District, Logar Province, Afghanistan. It was also the former capital of Logar Province. town is in a mountainous area in the valley of the Logar River. The main road Ghazni-Kabul passes about 20 km to the West of the town.
 Baraki Rajan: Baraki Rajan (Dari/Pashtun: برکی راجان) is a town within the Baraki Barak District of Logar Province, Afghanistan. Baraki Rajan lies approximately 3 km south of the town of Baraki Barak, the capital of the Baraki Barak District. Baraki Rajan is the location of the largest bazaar in the Baraki Barak District, with over 1,200 shops and businesses, with a 50+ bed hospital near town center, making Baraki Rajan an important center for commerce within District.
 Baraki Barak airstrike: The Baraki Barak airstrike was a coalition airstrike occurred on August 26, 2011 in Eastern Afghanistan. Six Afghan civilians from the same family were killed in air strike in the Baraki Barak district of Logar province, Afghanistan. Four insurgents and three Afghan army members were also killed.
 Logar Province: Logar (Pashto: لوګر ; Dari: لوگَر ) is one of the 34 provinces of Afghanistan, located in the eastern section of the country. It is divided into seven districts and contains hundreds of villages. Puli Alam is the capital of the province.
 Baraki Barak District: Baraki Barak District is situated in the western part of Logar Province, Afghanistan. It borders Wardak Province to west and northwest, Pul-i-Alam District to north and east and Kharwar and Charkh districts to the south. population is 101,000(2006). The district center is the town of Baraki Barak - the former provincial capital, located in the northern part of the district in the valley of the Logar River. Baraki Rajan is another important town of this district lies 4 km away from district center.
Mahsud: The Maseed, Mahsūd (Pashto: مسید، محسود ), also spelled Māsīd (Pashto: ماسيد ), is a Karlani Pashtun tribe inhabiting parts of the South Waziristan Agency in Federally Administered Tribal Areas of Pakistan. Maseed lineages are settled in the Logar Province of Afghanistan, especially in Charkh District, Baraki barak and Muhammad Agha, but also in Wardak, Ghazni and Kunduz Provinces. The Maseeds inhabit the center and north of South Waziristan valley, surrounded on three sides by the Darweshkhel Wazirs, shut off by the Bettanis on the east from the Derajat and Bannu districts. Two Pashtun tribes, the Ahmadzai Wazirs and the Maseeds, inhabit and dominate South Waziristan. Within the heart of Maseed territory in South Waziristan lies the influential Ormur (Burki) tribe's stronghold of Kaniguram. The Ormurs are considered by other tribes of South Waziristan to be close brethren of the Maseeds due to marital and other ties and the fact Ormurs have lived in and controlled Kaniguram for over a thousand years. There also some Maseeds living in the UAE, Germany and the United Kingdom.

Crescent Range: The Crescent Range, sometimes referred to as the Randolph Mountains, is located in the White Mountains of New Hampshire in the United States. The highest peak in range is Black Crescent Mountain, with an elevation of 3264 ft .
 Mount Crescent: Mount Crescent is a mountain located in the Crescent Range of the White Mountains in Randolph, New Hampshire. It is 3,251 ft (991 m) high, and its summit is the second highest mountain summit in Randolph, after Black Crescent Mountain (3,264 feet, 995 m). Both mountains are in Randolph's Ice Gulch Town Forest. On the 1896 topographic map, Mount Crescent is shown as "Randolph Mtn." with elevation of 3,280 ft, and Black Crescent is shown as "Mt. Crescent" with an elevation of 3,322 ft.
 Black Crescent Mountain: Black Crescent Mountain is a mountain in the Crescent Range of the White Mountains, 4.4 mi north of Randolph and 4.7 mi southwest of Berlin in New Hampshire. The summit is on the eastern boundary of the White Mountain National Forest.
 Santa Cruz (Santiago): Santa Cruz is a town in the eastern part of the island of Santiago, Cape Verde. It is located more than 2 kilometers southeast from the municipal seat of Santa Cruz Pedra Badejo on the road linking Praia and Tarrafal through Pedra Badejo, the EN1-ST02. it is situated over 30 km NNW of Praia. Its 2010 population was 2,019. Santa Cruz forms a part of the Pedra Badejo area which is about 20,000 people as of 2010. Santa Cruz's population are the top 20 and the top 25 populated places of the island which is larger than the oldest city on the island Cidade Velha, it is also the fourth most populated place in the municipality as of 2010.
 Mount Vernon, Indiana: Mount Vernon is a city in and the county seat of Posey County, Indiana, United States.Located in the state's far southwestern corner, within 15 miles of either the southernmost or westernmost points it is the westernmost city in the state, but not the southernmost, that being Rockport, about 40 miles to the southeast. The population was 6,687 at the 2010 census. It is located in Black Township and is part of the Evansville, Indiana, metropolitan area, which had a 2010 population of 358,676.
 Randolph, New Hampshire: Randolph is a heavily forested town in Coos County, New Hampshire, U.S., extending from the northern slopes of White Mountains of the Presidential Range (to the south) to the Crescent Range and Berlin (to the north), with U.S. Route 2 cutting through the middle. The northern and southern parts of Randolph are within the White Mountain National Forest and the Ice Gulch Town Forest, while the central part is the settled portion of town. As of the 2010 census, town had a total population of 310.

Stuart Roosa: Stuart Allen "Stu" Roosa (August 16, 1933 – December 12, 1994), (Col, USAF), was an American aeronautical engineer, United States Air Force pilot, test pilot, and NASA astronaut, was the Command Module Pilot for Apollo 14 mission. mission lasted from January 31 to February 9, 1971 was third mission to land astronauts (Alan Shepard and Edgar Mitchell) on the Moon. Shepard and Mitchell spent two days on lunar surface, Roosa conducted experiments from orbit in the Command Module "Kitty Hawk". He was one of only 24 people to travel to the Moon.
 Moon tree: Moon trees are trees grown from 500 seeds taken into orbit around Moon by Stuart Roosa during Apollo 14 mission in 1971. As Command Module Pilot on Apollo 14 mission, a former smoke jumper, Roosa contacted by Ed Cliff, Chief of the Forest Service at time, proposed the idea of taking seeds along. Seeds for experiment were chosen from five different types of trees: Loblolly Pine, Sycamore, Sweetgum, Redwood, and Douglas Fir.
 Apollo 16: Apollo 16 was tenth manned mission in the United States Apollo space program, fifth and penultimate to land on the Moon and first to land in the lunar highlands. second of the so-called "J missions," crewed by Commander John Young, Lunar Module Pilot Charles Duke and Command Module Pilot Ken Mattingly. Launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 12:54 PM EST on April 16, 1972, mission lasted 11 days, 1 hour, and 51 minutes, concluded at 2:45 PM EST on April 27.
 Apollo 8: Apollo 8, second human spaceflight mission in the United States Apollo space program, launched on December 21, 1968, became first crewed spacecraft to leave Earth orbit, reach Earth's Moon, orbit it and return safely to Earth.three-astronaut crew — Commander Frank Borman, Command Module Pilot James Lovell, and Lunar Module Pilot William Anders — became first humans to: travel beyond low Earth orbit; escape Earth's gravity; see Earth as a whole planet; enter gravity well of another celestial body (Earth's moon); orbit another celestial body (Earth's moon); directly see far side of Moon with their own eyes; witness an Earthrise; escape gravity of another celestial body (Earth's moon); re-enter gravitational well of Earth. 1968 mission, third flight of Saturn V rocket and rocket's first crewed launch, was also first human spaceflight launch from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, adjacent to Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
 Apollo 9: Apollo 9 was third manned mission in United States Apollo space program and first flight of Command/Service Module (CSM) with Lunar Module (LM, pronounced "lem"). three-person crew, consisting of Commander James McDivitt, Command Module Pilot David Scott, and Lunar Module Pilot Rusty Schweickart, spent ten days in low Earth orbit testing several aspects critical to landing on the Moon, including LM engines, backpack life support systems, navigation systems, and docking maneuvers. mission was second manned launch of Saturn V rocket.

Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. (film): Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. is an American television film based on Marvel Comics character Nick Fury. first broadcast on May 26, 1998 on Fox. Directed by Rod Hardy, film stars David Hasselhoff as Fury, a retired super spy approached to return to duty to take down terrorist organization HYDRA, threaten to attack Manhattan with a pathogen reconstituted known as Death's Head virus. Lisa Rinna plays Contessa Valentina "Val" Allegra de Fontaine, and Sandra Hess plays Andrea von Strucker / Viper. released on DVD on September 30, 2008.
 Nick Fury (2017 comic book): Nick Fury is a 2017 ongoing comic book series published by Marvel Comics. series written by James Dale Robinson primarily drawn by ACO. first series to feature Nick Fury Jr. as main character.
 Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. (feature): Nick Fury, Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. was a feature on in anthology comic "Strange Tales" introduced fictional spy agency S.H.I.E.L.D. into Marvel Comics world and reintroduced character of Nick Fury as older character from currently running series "Sgt. Fury", was a WWII comic. feature replaced previously running Human Torch feature in book and ran alongside Dr. Strange feature. After feature ended a comic title was published had several volumes as as a comic strip.
 Fenris (comics): Andrea von Strucker and Andreas von Strucker are two fictional characters appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. They are the German twin children of supervillain Baron von Strucker of HYDRA and half-siblings of Werner von Strucker.
Ultimate Nick Fury: General Nicholas Joseph "Nick" Fury is a fictional character appearing in comic books published by Marvel Comics' Ultimate Marvel section as different version of Nick Fury or Nick Fury Jr., his son and successor as director of S.H.I.E.L.D. He substantial presence in all Ultimate Marvel comics, appearing first in "Ultimate Marvel Team-Up" and "Ultimate X-Men" later reappearing regularly in "Ultimate Spider-Man" finally securing regular, recurring role as general of S.H.I.E.L.D. and leader of the Ultimates, re-imagining of the Avengers character designed to look like Samuel L. Jackson, actor who later portray Nick Fury in several Marvel movies and television shows set in established Marvel Cinematic Universe.

College Humor (film): College Humor 1933 American pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Wesley Ruggles starring Bing Crosby Jack Oakie Richard Arlen Mary Kornman Mary Carlisle. Based on story by Dean Fales film about college professor school's star football player rivals for same beautiful coed. Released by Paramount Pictures film co-stars George Burns Gracie Allen.
 Going Hollywood: 1933 American pre-Code musical film directed by Raoul Walsh starring Marion Davies Bing Crosby written by Donald Ogden Stewart based on story by Frances Marion Hollywood released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer December 22, 1933.
 Bing Crosby: Harry Lillis "Bing" Crosby Jr ( ; May 3, 1903 – October 14, 1977) American singer actor. Crosby's trademark warm bass-baritone voice made him best-selling recording artist of 20th century sold over one billion records, tapes compact discs digital downloads.
 Hallelujah, I'm a Bum (film): 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film directed by Lewis Milestone set in Great Depression.
 My Lips Betray: 1933 American Pre-Code musical comedy film directed by John G. Blystone starring Lilian Harvey John Boles El Brendel. film sets designed by art director Joseph C. Wright.
 International House (1933 film): International House 1933 American pre-Code comedy film starring Peggy Hopkins Joyce W. C. Fields directed by A. Edward Sutherland released by Paramount Pictures. tagline "The Grand Hotel of comedy". mixture of comedy musical acts by slim plot line style of Big Broadcast pictures released by Paramount during 1930s. typical comedic lunacy from W. C.Fields and Burns Allen, provides snapshot of popular stage and radio acts of era. film includes risqué pre-Code humor.

Fred C. Koch: Fred Chase Koch ( ; September 23, 1900 – November 17, 1967) was American chemical engineer and entrepreneur founded oil refinery firm later became Koch Industries, a privately held company under principal ownership leadership of Koch's sons, Charles and David, listed by "Forbes," as of 2015, as second-largest privately held company in United States.
 Koch family foundations: Koch family foundations are group of charitable foundations in United States associated with family of Fred C. Koch. prominent are Charles Koch Foundation and David H. Koch Charitable Foundation, created by Charles Koch and David Koch, two sons of Fred C. Koch own majority of Koch Industries, an oil, gas, paper, and chemical conglomerate US's second-largest privately held company. Charles' and David's foundations provided millions of dollars to organizations, including libertarian and conservative think tanks. Areas of funding include think tanks, political advocacy, climate change scepticism, higher education scholarships, cancer research, arts, and science.
 Dark Money (book): Dark Money: The Hidden History of the Billionaires Behind the Rise of the Radical Right (2016) is non-fiction book written by American investigative journalist Jane Mayer, about network of wealthy conservative libertarians, Charles and David Koch, funded organizations to influence academic institutions, think tanks, courts, statehouses, Congress, American presidency for benefit. Mayer discusses Koch family their political activities, along with Richard Mellon Scaife and John M. Olin funded American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), DeVos and Coors families.
 Koch family: Koch family ( ) is an American family engaged in business noted for political activities and control of Koch Industries, second-largest privately owned company in United States (with 2013 revenues of $115 billion). family business started by Fred C.Koch, developed new cracking method for refinement of heavy crude oil into gasoline. Fred's four sons litigated against each other over interests in business during 1980s and 1990s.
 David Koch: David Hamilton Koch ( ; born May 3, 1940) is American businessman, philanthropist, political activist, chemical engineer. joined family business Koch Industries, conglomerate second-largest privately held company in United States, in 1970. became president of subsidiary Koch Engineering in 1979, a co-owner of Koch Industries, with older brother Charles, in 1983. now executive vice president. Koch an influential libertarian was 1980 candidate for Vice President of United States from United States Libertarian Party helped finance campaign. founded Citizens for a Sound Economy. He and brother Charles donated to political advocacy groups and to political campaigns, almost entirely Republican.

New York State Route 9R: New York State Route 9R (NY 9R) is a north–south state highway in northeastern Albany County, New York, in the United States. route is a 3.22 mi eastern loop of U.S. Route 9 (US 9), connecting route to city of Cohoes 1.5 mi to the east. It leaves US 9 in the hamlet of Latham and rejoins its parent in the hamlet of Boght Corners, both located in the town of Colonie. Most of NY 9R is a two-lane highway passes through residential areas; southwesternmost portion of route is four lanes wide and serves a commercial district route was assigned c. 1939 and remained largely unchanged since, save for a brief period during 1970s where NY 9R was partially replaced by NY 470.
 Boght Corners, New York: Boght Corners (also referred to as Boght) is a hamlet in the town of Colonie in northern Albany County, New York straddles U.S. Route 9 (Route 9). corners give hamlet its name are found at the intersection of Route 9 and Boght Road (NY Route 9R on leg east of hamlet), near Boght Community Fire District’s station. community is served by North Colonie Central School District. Boght Hills Elementary School is located within the hamlet.
 New York State Route 9N: New York State Route 9N (NY 9N) is a north–south state highway in northeastern New York in the United States. It extends from intersection with U.S. Route 9 (US 9), NY 29, and NY 50 in the city of Saratoga Springs to a junction with US 9 and NY 22 in the Clinton County hamlet of Keeseville. At 143.49 mi in total length, NY 9N is the longest letter-suffixed route in the state is concurrent with its parent route for 1 mi in the village of Lake George and for three blocks in the hamlet of Elizabethtown.
Borodino, New York: Borodino is a hamlet located at the intersection of New York State Route 41 (East Lake Road, running east-west) and New York State Route 174 (Rose Hill Road, running north-south) in the Town of Spafford in Onondaga County, New York, near Skaneateles Lake. hamlet extends five to ten properties to east, south, west and north from intersection, until houses and other buildings replaced by farm fields. A monument for veterans, designed by Gianfranco Fritelli, stands in a cemetery at the southeast corner of intersection. A little-altered Federal style Methodist Church, known locally as "The Church", dating from 1830, stands close to the 174, about five properties north. Borodino District School No. 8 (c. 1853–59) and Borodino Hall (1835) are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
 New York State Route 9B: New York State Route 9B (NY 9B) is a state highway within Clinton County, New York, in the United States. route serves as a connector between its parent route, U.S. Route 9 (US 9), in the town of Champlain and US 11 in the village of Rouses Point. While US 9 bypasses Rouses Point to west, NY 9B veers east to serve village and shoreline of Lake Champlain. NY 9B is northernmost section of the Lakes to Locks Passage, an All-American Road. Modern NY 9B was the original alignment of US 9 through the town of Champlain. US 9 was moved onto its present alignment west of Rouses Point in the mid-1940s, its former routing to Rouses Point became NY 9B.

12 Years a Slave (score): 12 Years a Slave is the original soundtrack album to 2013 film "12 Years a Slave" starring Chiwetel Ejiofor, Michael Fassbender, Benedict Cumberbatch, Paul Dano, and Lupita Nyong'o. record contains twenty-one tracks from original film score written and composed by Hans Zimmer. The score was widely admired and thought of as a contender for the Academy Award for Original Music Score at the 86th Academy Awards.
 Chiwetel Ejiofor: Chiwetel Umeadi Ejiofor, CBE ( ; born 10 July 1977) is a British actor. After enrolling at the National Youth Theatre in 1995, gaining a scholarship to the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art, at age 19 and three months into course, Ejiofor was cast by Steven Spielberg to play supporting role in the film "Amistad" (1997) as James Covey.
 Schapelle Corby: Schapelle Leigh Corby (born 10 July 1977) is an Australian woman was convicted of smuggling cannabis into Indonesia. She spent nine years imprisoned on the Indonesian island of Bali in Kerobokan Prison. Since her arrest Corby has publicly maintained drugs were planted in her bodyboard bag and she did not know about them. Her trial and conviction were a major focus of attention for Australian media.
 Levan Kobiashvili: Levan Kobiashvili (Georgian: ლევან კობიაშვილი , born 10 July 1977) is a retired Georgian footballer and current president of the Georgian Football Federation.
 José Marcos Garay: José Marcos Garay Álvarez (born 10 July 1977) is a Mexican footballer. currently plays for Tecos in the Mexican First Division.

Taj Mahal Bangladesh: Taj Mahal Bangladesh (Bengali: তাজ মহল বাংলাদেশ )is a scaled copy of original Taj Mahal (a Mughal mausoleum located in Agra, India) 10 miles east of Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka in Sonargaon. Unlike original, work on building took five years. Ahsanullah Moni, a wealthy Bangladeshi film-maker, announced his 'Copycat version of Taj Mahal' project in December 2008. project cost USD$56 Million, built 20 miles northeast of Capital Dhaka. Moni explained built replica of Taj Mahal so poor of his nation can realise dream of seeing neighbouring India's famed monument. caused complaints from Indian officials, "You can't copy historical monuments" official of Indian High Commission in Dhaka told press.
 Agra Fort: Agra Fort is a historical fort in city of Agra in India. was main residence of emperors of Mughal Dynasty till 1638, when capital shifted from Agra to Delhi. Agra fort is a UNESCO World Heritage site. about 2.5 km northwest of famous sister monument, Taj Mahal. fort described as a walled city.
 The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel (Marathi: ताजमहल हॉटेल) is a "Heritage Grand" class five-star hotel in Colaba region of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, next to Gateway of India. Historically was known as "Taj Mahal Hotel" or "Taj Palace Hotel". or simply "the Taj".
 Black Taj Mahal: Black Taj Mahal ("Black Taj", "Kaala Taj", also "the 2nd Taj") is a legendary black marble mausoleum said to planned to be built across Yamuna River opposite Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India. Mughal emperor Shah Jahan said to desired a mausoleum for himself similar to one built in memory of his third wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
Taj Mahal, Bulandshahar: Taj Mahal Mini Taj Mahal Qadri's Taj Mahal officially known as Maqbara Yadgare Mohabbat Tajammuli Begum is replica of historic Taj Mahal of Agra in Kaser Kalan, small village in Bulandshahar Uttar Pradesh India built by 81 years old retired postmaster Faizul Hasan Qadri in memory of dead wife Tajamulli Begum died due to throat cancer in 2011.

Franco Corelli: Franco Corelli (8 April 1921 – 29 October 2003) was Italian tenor had major international opera career between 1951 and 1976. Associated with spinto and dramatic tenor roles of Italian repertory celebrated universally for powerhouse voice, electrifying top notes clear timbre passionate singing remarkable performances. Dubbed "Prince of tenors", Corelli possessed handsome features charismatic stage presence endeared him to audiences. had long fruitful partnership with Metropolitan Opera in New York City between 1961 and 1975. appeared on stages of most major opera houses in Europe with opera companies throughout North America.
 Tosca (1956 film): Tosca is 1956 Italian musical film directed by Carmine Gallone starring Franca Duval, Afro Poli Franco Corelli. based on opera "Tosca" by Giacomo Puccini. made at Cinecittà in Rome.
 La Bohème (1988 film): La bohème (also known as "La bohème de Puccini") is 1988 Italian-French film of opera directed by Luigi Comencini based on Giacomo Puccini's "La bohème".
 Jacopo Puccini: Jacopo (Giacomo) Puccini (] ; 26 January 1712 16 May 1781) was 18th-century Italian composer lived worked primarily in Lucca, Tuscany. first of five generations of composers, most famous was his great-great-grandson, opera composer Giacomo Puccini.
 Gianni Schicchi: Gianni Schicchi (] ) is comic opera in one act by Giacomo Puccini to Italian libretto by Giovacchino Forzano composed in 1917–18. libretto based on incident mentioned in Dante's "Divine Comedy". work is third and final part of Puccini's "Il trittico" (The Triptych)—three one-act operas with contrasting themes originally written to be presented together.continues to performed with one or both other "trittico" operas, "Gianni Schicchi" now more frequently staged alone or with short operas by other composers. aria "O mio babbino caro" is one of Puccini's best known, and one of most popular arias in opera.
 Ron Bottcher: Ron Bottcher (11 May 1940 – 12 April 1991) was American operatic baritone actively performing with New York City Opera (NYCO) and Metropolitan Opera during 1960s. native of Sandpoint, Idaho earned music degrees from University of Montana and Curtis Institute of Music. debut at Santa Fe Opera in summer of 1961, portrayed roles of Leopold in Richard Strauss' "Der Rosenkavalier", Marcello in Giacomo Puccini's "La bohème", Head waiter in Paul Hindemith's "Neues vom Tage". roles at NYCO included Escamillo in Georges Bizet's "Carmen" and Sharpless in Puccini's "Madama Butterfly" others. At Met created roles in world premieres of Samuel Barber's "Antony and Cleopatra" and Marvin David Levy's "Mourning Becomes Electra". died at age of 50 at Lenox Hill Hospital in Manhattan of AIDS related illness.

Project African Wilderness: Project African Wilderness (PAW) is a not for profit organisation purpose protecting restoring Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve in Malawi.
 Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve: area of 135km2 Mwabvi Wildlife Reserve is Malawi’s smallest national park least accessible. has wide variety of habitats, including Mopane, Combretum brachystegia woodland open savanna, dambo, riverine areas. Mwabvi was last natural home to Malawi's Black Rhino population, wildlife and woodland poached over recent years. many species of antelope, including kudu, sable, impala nyala, present, leopard and hyena seen. Buffalo bathe in Mwabvi river number of human tourists low, lions from neighbouring Mozambique are regular visitors. scenery is spectacular views over Shire River and Zambesi river, magnificent sandstone outcrops give almost lunar feel to landscape.
 African buffalo: African buffalo or Cape buffalo ("Syncerus caffer") is a large African bovine. not closely related to larger wild water buffalo of Asia ancestry unclear. "Syncerus caffer Cape buffalo typical subspecies largest one, found in South and East Africa. "S. c. nanus" (African forest buffalo) is smallest subspecies common in forest areas of Central and West Africa "S. c. brachyceros" in West Africa and "S. c. aequinoctialis" in savannas of East Africa. adult buffalo's horns are characteristic feature fused bases forming continuous bone shield across top of head referred to as a "boss". regarded as dangerous animals, they gore and kill over 200 people every year.
Saint-Maurice Wildlife Reserve: is a 782 km2 wildlife reserve north of Shawinigan. reserve located west of Saint-Maurice River in territory of Mekinac Regional County Municipality. Like all wildlife reserves area dedicated to conservation, development use of wildlife practice of recreational activity. not considered a protected area; forest and mining activities are allowed.
 Sir Bani Yas: Sir (Arabic: صير بنى ياس ) is a natural island 170 km southwest of Abu Dhabi, capital of United Arab Emirates. 9 km offshore from Jebel Dhanna crossing point to other islands Dalma (island). Sir Bani Yas is 17.5 km from north to south 9 km from east to west largest natural island in United Arab Emirates. off shore of Western region of Abu Dhabi Sir Bani Yas island was originally home to Arabia's largest wildlife reserve. Spanning over 87 km2, reserve established in 1977 by Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al Nahyan. Thanks to decades of conservation work ecological investment now home to thousands of large free-roaming animals several million trees and plants. bird sanctuary wildlife reserve, Sir Bani Yas showcases nature through activities adventure safaris, kayaking, mountain biking archery hiking snorkeling.

New Orleans Pelicans: New Orleans Pelicans are an American professional basketball team based in New Orleans, Louisiana. Pelicans compete in National Basketball Association (NBA) as member club of league's Western Conference Southwest Division. team plays home games in the Smoothie King Center (formerly known as the New Orleans Arena).
 Jalen Jones: Jalen Jones (born May 27, 1993) is an American professional basketball player for New Orleans Pelicans of National Basketball Association (NBA). He signed on a two-way contract with NBA G League. played college basketball for Southern Methodist and Texas A&M.
 Portland Trail Blazers: Portland Trail Blazers, commonly known as the Blazers, are an American professional basketball team based in Portland, Oregon. Trail Blazers compete in National Basketball Association (NBA) as member club of league's Western Conference Northwest Division. team played home games in Memorial Coliseum before moving to Moda Center in 1995 (called the Rose Garden until 2013). franchise entered league as an expansion team in 1970, enjoyed strong following: from 1977 through 1995, team sold out 814 consecutive home games, the longest such streak in American major professional sports at time, only since surpassed by Boston Red Sox. Trail Blazers have been only NBA team based in bi-national Pacific Northwest, after Vancouver Grizzlies relocated to Memphis and became Memphis Grizzlies in 2001, and Seattle SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City became Oklahoma City Thunder in 2008.
 Erie BayHawks (2017–): Erie BayHawks are an American professional basketball team of the NBA G League and an affiliate of Atlanta Hawks of the National Basketball Association. Based in Erie, Pennsylvania, team will play home games during 2017–18 and 2018–19 seasons at the Erie Insurance Arena. Atlanta Hawks plan to relocate G League franchise to College Park, Georgia, before 2019–20 season to play at new arena in Georgia International Convention Center. team became the sixteenth D-League team to be owned by an NBA team.
Portland Trail Blazers all-time roster: Portland Trail Blazers, commonly known as the Blazers, are an American professional basketball team based in Portland, Oregon. They play in the Northwest Division of Western Conference in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Trail Blazers originally played home games in Memorial Coliseum, before moving to Rose Garden in 1995. franchise entered league in 1970, Portland has its only home city. franchise has enjoyed strong following; from 1977 through 1995, team sold out 814 consecutive home games, the longest such streak in American major professional sports. Trail Blazers are only team in the major professional North American sports leagues located in state of Oregon Trail Blazers are also currently only NBA team based in the binational Pacific Northwest, after Vancouver Grizzlies relocated to Memphis and became Memphis Grizzlies in 2001, and Seattle SuperSonics relocated to Oklahoma City became Oklahoma City Thunder in 2008.

Blues Traveler: Blues is American rock band formed in Princeton, New Jersey in 1987. band's music covers variety of genres, including blues rock, psychedelic rock, folk rock soul, Southern rock known for extensive use of segues in live performances key part of re-emerging jam band scene of 1990s spearheading H.O.R.D.E. touring music festival.
 Bridge (Blues Traveler album): Bridge is sixth album by American jam band Blues Traveler released May 2001 (see 2001 in music). Blues Traveler's first album following 1999 death of bassist Bobby Sheehan. album originally titled "Bridge Out of Brooklyn."
 Blues Traveler (album): Blues Traveler eponymous debut album from Blues Traveler released on A&M Records in 1990. establishes band's trademark jam band sound featuring John Popper's harmonica.
 Travelers and Thieves: Travelers and Thieves is Blues Traveler's second album released on A&M Records in 1991. album released in two versions: album-only version, and limited two-CD pressing. bonus disc called "On Tour Forever". On iTunes album listed only as "Travelers" due to full name split across two drawings, one on cover and one inside CD liner notes.
 On Tour Forever: On Tour Forever is live EP album released by Blues Traveler in 1992. Only ten thousand copies produced packaged as double album with copies of band's second album, "Travelers and Thieves".
 Blues Brothers 2000 (soundtrack): Blues Brothers 2000: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is third studio album by The Blues Brothers, twelfth release, overall.It soundtrack album to 1998 film, "Blues Brothers 2000", sequel to 1980 film, "The Blues Brothers". In addition to tracks by Blues Brothers Band and guest artists as Aretha Franklin, James Brown, Eddie Floyd Wilson Pickett, songs by Paul Butterfield Blues Band and Blues Traveler all-star blues supergroup, Louisiana Gator Boys, featuring B.B. King, Eric Clapton, Bo Diddley, Charlie Musselwhite, Doctor John, Lou Rawls, Koko Taylor, Isaac Hayes, Billy Preston other artists.

Kinnaird Castle, Brechin: Kinnaird Castle is a 15th-century castle in Angus, Scotland castle been home to Carnegie family, the Earl of Southesk, for more than 600 years.
 Lady Charlotte Elliot: Lady Charlotte Elliot (22 July 1839 – 15 January 1880), born Charlotte Carnegie, was a Victorian poet born on 22 July 1839 in parish of Farnell, Angus (possibly at Kinnaird Castle), Scotland.
 Fra Lippo Lippi (poem): Fra Lippo Lippi is an 1855 dramatic monologue written by Victorian poet Robert Browning first appeared in his collection "Men and Women". poem, Browning depicts 15th-century real-life painter, Filippo Lippi. poem asks question whether art should be true to life or idealized image of life. poem written in blank verse, non-rhyming iambic pentameter.
 Megginch Castle: Megginch Castle is a 15th-century castle in Perth and Kinross, in central Scotland. was family home of late Cherry Drummond, 16th Baroness Strange. now occupied by Lady Strange's daughter Catherine Star Violetta Herdman and her husband.
 Dundas Castle: Dundas Castle is a 15th-century castle, with substantial 19th-century additions by William Burn, in Dalmeny parish of West Lothian, Scotland. home of Dundas family since Middle Ages, sold in late 19th century and currently residence of politician and businessman Sir Jack Stewart-Clark.
 Hayashi Castle: Hayashi castle was a 15th-century castle, (alternatively known as Hayashi-jo, Fukuyama-jo) in Satoyamabe village, Matsumoto city, Nagano, Japan. mountain-type castle, now largely in ruins. site sometimes regarded as one castle, or two castles, Hayashikojo (the small castle) and Hayashiohjo (the larger castle).

Battle of Berlin Battle Berlin Berlin Strategic Offensive Operation by Soviet Union final major offensive European theatre of World War II.
 Alexander Nikolayev Alexander Petrovich Nikolayev (Russian: Александр Петрович Николаев; 14 November 1918 – 13 June 2009) Red Army senior lieutenant Hero of Soviet Union. received title Hero of Soviet Union Order of Lenin for actions during Battle of Berlin. Nikolayev fought in Siege of Leningrad.
 Mikhail Linnik Mikhail Nikiforovich Linnik (Russian: Михаил Никифорович Линник; 25 October 1916 – 21 December 2007) Soviet Army captain Hero of Soviet Union. Linnik awarded title Hero of Soviet Union Order of Lenin for actions Lublin–Brest Offensive September 1944.
 Georgy Vasilyevich Ivanov Georgy Vasilyevich Ivanov (Russian: Георгий Васильевич Иванов; 25 May 1901 – 25 December 2001) Soviet Army major general Hero of Soviet Union. Ivanov awarded title Hero of Soviet Union Order of Lenin leadership of 6th Guards Rifle Division late 1944 to 1945. Ivanov fought in World War II Battle of the Dnieper Vistula–Oder Offensive.
 Vladimir Fedorovich Vladimirov Vladimir Fedorovich Vladimirov (Russian Владимир Фёдорович Владимиров; 9 July 1914 – December 1943) Red Army Lieutenant during World War II Hero of Soviet Union. posthumously awarded title Hero of Soviet Union Order of Lenin for actions during Battle of the Dnieper. Vladimirov killed in action December 1943.
 Anatoly Petrakovsky: Anatoly Iosifovich Petrakovsky (Russian: Анатолий Иосифович Петраковский; 28 December 1901 – 3 September 1969) Ukrainian Soviet Army major general Hero of the Soviet Union. joining Red Army in 1922 Petrakovsky became officer rose through ranks eve of Winter War battalion commander in 13th Rifle Division.Petrakovsky awarded title Hero of Soviet Union and Order of Lenin for leadership of battalion. After Operation Barbarossa became commander of 395th Rifle Division. led division during Battle of Rostov and Battle of Voronezh relieved of command due to "systemic failure to comply with orders". In August 1943 Petrakovsky became commander of 57th Rifle Corps lost command corps sent to hospital receive treatment for illness. After graduating from Military Academy of General Staff, appointed deputy commander of 16th Army participated in Invasion of South Sakhalin. Postwar Petrakovsky served in various staff positions retired in 1956.
 Boris Vladimirov: Boris Alexandrovich Vladimirov (Russian: Борис Александрович Владимиров ; 14 April 1905 – 1 May 1978) was Soviet Army lieutenant general Hero of Soviet Union. Vladimirov served in Russian Civil War after drafted into Red Army in 1921. became officer by 1941 deputy regimental commander. After German invasion of Soviet Union Vladimirov became senior officer in charge of formation of march battalions in Siberian Military District, chief of staff of ski brigade, and rifle brigade. commanded rifle brigade in Siege of Leningrad, during Lyuban Offensive Operation Sinyavino Offensive. Vladimirov took command of 311th Rifle Division in March 1943 leading it until end of war. awarded title Hero of Soviet Union for leadership in Vistula–Oder Offensive. Postwar Vladimirov became lieutenant general commanded rifle corps deputy chief of staff of Soviet airborne. retired in 1960 lived in Moscow.

Cale Gundy: Joseph Cale Gundy (born April 10, 1972) is former American football quarterback played for Oklahoma Sooners from 1990 to 1993. While at Oklahoma was a member of Delta Tau Delta International Fraternity. After coaching running backs for 16 years at Oklahoma Gundy promoted to Assistant Head Coach moved to Inside Receivers for 2015 season. His brother, Mike, is head football coach at Oklahoma State University.
 Mike Gundy: Mike Gundy (born August 12, 1967) is an American football coach and former player. currently the head football coach at Oklahoma State University. Gundy played college football at Oklahoma State, played quarterback from 1986 to 1989. became Oklahoma State's coach on January 3, 2005. In 2007, received national media attention for his heated criticism of newspaper article on one of his players.
 Ike Mahoney: Frank John Mahoney Jr. (October 25, 1901 – November 21, 1961) was American football back played five seasons with Chicago Cardinals of National Football League. played college football at Creighton University and attended Omaha High School of Commerce in Omaha, Nebraska. a member of Chicago Cardinals team were NFL champions in 1925. also played baseball, basketball and participated in track and field. Mahoney played for Chicago Bruins of American Basketball League. had received offer to play baseball for Pittsburgh Pirates but opted to play football for Chicago Cardinals.
 Ben Coates: Ben Terrence Coates (born August 16, 1969) is former American football tight end in National Football League and former CIAA football coach and former NFL tight ends coach. Coates didn't play football until senior year at Greenwood High School, was a multi-sport player at Livingstone College located in Salisbury, North Carolina. As gridiron player at Livingstone, broke nearly all meaningful records at school, but due to split-sport performances, against weak competition, for non-notable school, received little notice outside of CIAA. While a college student, joined Phi Beta Sigma fraternity through Upsilon Chapter at Livingstone College.
Bob Adams (American football): Robert Bruce "Bob" Adams (born August 15, 1946) is a former professional American football tight end in National Football League (NFL) and spokesperson for Church of Scientology International. attended El Camino High School during 1960s, encouraged by coach at College of San Mateo to play football. played for a single season at college, during 1966, participating in other sports at school including track-and-field and basketball. former coach of College of San Mateo, Doug Scovil, recruited Adams to College of the Pacific, received full scholarship to play football there. By 1968, was captain of team's offense at school.
 Chris Rubio: Chris Rubio is American trainer of long snappers in American football. works with high school long snappers and evaluates them for college football programs. His Rubio’s Long Snapping camp is the longest running in nation. Over past 12 years, Rubio helped over 500 long snappers play football in college and NFL. Rubio partners with Chris Sailer, provides similar service for placekickers and punters with Chris Sailer Kicking. two were teammates in college with UCLA Bruins.
 Indoor soccer: Indoor soccer, or arena soccer (known internationally as indoor football, minifootball, fast football, floorball or showball), is a game derived from association football adapted for play in walled indoor arena. Indoor soccer, most often known in United States and Canada, originally developed in these two countries as way to play football during winter months, when snow make outdoor play difficult. In those countries, areas such as hockey rinks or basketball courts are adapted for indoor soccer play. In other countries game is played in either indoor or outdoor arenas surrounded by walls, referred to by different names (such as "fast football" (futbol rapido) in Mexico, "showbol" in South America, and "indoor football" (futbol indoor) in Spain).

Nick Carter (musician): Nickolas Gene "Nick" Carter (born January 28, 1980) is an American singer, songwriter, actor, and dancer. best known as member of pop group Backstreet Boys. As of 2015, Carter released three solo albums, "Now or Never", "I'm Taking Off" and "All American" during breaks between Backstreet Boys schedules, and a collaboration with Jordan Knight titled "Nick & Knight". made occasional television appearances and starred in own reality shows, "House of Carters" and "I (Heart) Nick Carter". gained fame in mid 1990s and early 2000s as teen idol. also older brother of singer Aaron Carter and late Leslie Carter.
 Brady Seals: Brady Seals (born March 29, 1969) is an American country music artist. cousin of Jim Seals (of Seals & Crofts) and Dan Seals and Johnny Duncan, nephew of Troy Seals, and husband of former BNA Records recording artist Lisa Stewart. Seals made debut in 1988 as co-lead vocalist and keyboardist in sextet Little Texas, with recorded until departure in late 1994. Between then and 2002, recorded as solo singer, releasing three studio albums charting in Top 40 on country charts with "Another You, Another Me". In 2002, Seals formed a quartet called Hot Apple Pie, in recorded one studio album and charted three singles. fourth solo album, "Play Time", released in 2009 via Star City.
 Brady Seals (album): Brady Seals is self-titled second album by American country music singer Brady Seals. his second release independently of band Little Texas, of he was a member until 1995. album includes singlse "I Fell", "Whole Lotta Hurt" and "The Best Is Yet to Come". All three singles charted on "Billboard" country charts, although all missed Top 40.
The Truth (Brady Seals album): The Truth is debut studio album of American country music singer Brady Seals, his first solo album after leaving country band Little Texas released on February 25, 1997 on Reprise Records. album includes singles "Another You, Another Me", "Still Standing Tall", and "Natural Born Lovers". only "Another You, Another Me" reached Top 40 on Hot Country Songs. Seals co-wrote all but two of album's songs, co-produced album with Rodney Crowell.

Bayezid II Mosque (Amasya): Bayezid II Mosque (Amasya) is a historical 15th century Mosque in Amasya, Turkey. mosque was built in 1486 by order of the Ottoman sultan Bayezid II, it is the largest Külliye of the city.
 Beyazıt Square: Beyazıt Square (Turkish: "Beyazıt Meydanı" ) is a square in district of Fatih, situated in the European part of Istanbul, Turkey. It is officially named "Freedom Square" ("Hürriyet Meydanı" ), but is known as Beyazıt Square after Bayezid II Mosque on one side of it. Square is former site of Forum of Theodosius built by Constantine the Great. On one side of square is the main entrance of Istanbul University; the Beyazıt Tower is on the university's campus and can be seen from the square. current form of square was designed by Turgut Cansever.
 Gazi Atik Ali Pasha Mosque: The Gazi Atik Ali Pasha Mosque (Turkish: "Gazi Atik Ali Paşa Camii" ) is an old Ottoman mosque located in the Çemberlitaş neighbourhood of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. Its construction started under orders of future Grand Vizier Hadım Atik Ali Pasha in 1496 and completed in 1497, during reign of Sultan Bayezid II. mosque is located near the entrance to Kapalıçarşı (Grand Bazaar), the Column of Constantine, and historical Nuruosmaniye Mosque.
 Bayezid II Mosque: The Bayezid II Mosque (Turkish: "Beyazıt Camii, Bayezid Camii" ) is an Ottoman imperial mosque located in the Beyazıt Square area of Istanbul, Turkey, near the ruins of the Forum of Theodosius of ancient Constantinople.
 Nusretiye Mosque: Nusretiye Mosque is an ornate mosque located in Tophane district of Beyoğlu, Istanbul, Turkey. its architecture is influenced by Islamic elements, it retains a Baroque style, making it unique to the city. It was built in 1823-1826 by Sultan Mahmut II.

 Vasat Atik Ali Pasha Mosque: Vasat Atik Ali Pasha Mosque (Turkish: "Vasat Atik Ali Paşa Camii" ), also known as Zincirlikuyu Mosque (Turkish: "Zincirlikuyu Camii" ) or Karagümrük Mosque, is an Ottoman mosque located in the Karagümrük neighbourhood of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey, on Fevzipaşa Street. Sultan Bayezid II's grand vizier Hadım Atik Ali Pasha, after mosque is named, ordered its construction in 1502, completed in 1512, one year after the grand vizier's death.

Greg Monroe: Gregory Keith Monroe Jr. (born June 4, 1990) is an American professional basketball player for Milwaukee Bucks of National Basketball Association (NBA). In his freshman season at Georgetown University, Monroe was named Big East Rookie of the Year. He drafted by Detroit Pistons in 2010 NBA draft with seventh overall pick became last Pistons player to wear #10 jersey, after Pistons retired number for Dennis Rodman at halftime of game against Chicago Bulls on April 1, 2011.
 Jerome Williams (basketball): Jerome Williams (born May 10, 1973) is an American retired professional basketball player last played for New York Knicks of the NBA. was a star player on Magruder High School basketball team. Drafted out of Georgetown University by Detroit Pistons with 26th pick of 1996 NBA Draft (the pick originally belonged to San Antonio Spurs and went to Pistons in Dennis Rodman trade), he played four-plus years with Pistons, becoming one of their key reserves. was a fan favorite during days playing for Toronto Raptors due to his tenacious efforts on the court.
 Detroit Pistons: Detroit Pistons are an American professional basketball team based in Detroit, Michigan. Pistons compete in the National Basketball Association (NBA) as a member club of league's Eastern Conference Central Division. team plays home games at Little Caesars Arena founded in Fort Wayne, Indiana as Fort Wayne (Zollner) Pistons in 1941, member of National Basketball League (NBL). Pistons joined the Basketball Association of America (BAA) in 1948. In 1949, NBL and BAA merged to become NBA, Pistons became part of merged league. Since moving to Detroit in 1957, Pistons have won three NBA championships in 1989, 1990 and 2004.
Dennis Rodman: Dennis Keith Rodman (born May 13, 1961) is an American retired professional basketball player, played for Detroit Pistons, San Antonio Spurs, Chicago Bulls, Los Angeles Lakers, and Dallas Mavericks in National Basketball Association (NBA). nicknamed "The Worm" known for his fierce defensive and rebounding abilities.
 Chauncey Billups: Chauncey Ray Billups (born September 25, 1976) is American retired professional basketball player played 17 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA). A star at University of Colorado, selected third overall in 1997 NBA draft by Boston Celtics. five-time NBA All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection, Billups played for Celtics, Toronto Raptors, Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Detroit Pistons, New York Knicks, Los Angeles Clippers during his NBA career. won NBA Finals MVP in 2004 after helping Pistons beat Los Angeles Lakers in Finals, given nickname "Mr. Big Shot" for making late-game shots with Detroit. Pistons retired his number #1 jersey in 2016.
 2005–06 Detroit Pistons season: 2005–06 Detroit Pistons season was 65th season of the franchise, 58th in National Basketball Association (NBA), and 49th in the Detroit area. Pistons began season hoping to improve upon 54–28 output from previous season have another chance of going to NBA Finals after losing to San Antonio Spurs in last season's NBA Finals in seven games. They bested it by ten games, finishing 64–18—their best record in franchise history—and qualifying for playoffs for the fifth straight season. Pistons defeated Milwaukee Bucks in five games in first round, and Cleveland Cavaliers in tough hard fought seven game series to reached the Eastern Conference Finals for fourth consecutive year before losing to eventual NBA champions Miami Heat, whom they had beaten in a seven-game playoff series the year before.Detroit's offseason marked by departure of star defensive player Ben Wallace, who signed a free-agent deal with Chicago Bulls.

Valens Aqueduct: Aqueduct (Turkish: "Valens Su Kemeri" or "Bozdoğan Kemeri" "Aqueduct of the Grey Falcon"; Ancient Greek: Ἀγωγὸς τοῦ ὕδατος  "Agōgós tou hýdatos", "aqueduct") is Roman aqueduct major water-providing system of Eastern Roman capital Constantinople (modern Istanbul, Turkey). Completed by Roman Emperor Valens late 4th century AD maintained used by Byzantines later Ottomans remains one of important landmarks of city.
 Atik Valide Mosque: (Turkish: "Atik Valide Camii, Eski Valide Camii" ) Ottoman mosque on hill above large densely populated district of Üsküdar, in Istanbul, Turkey.
 New Mosque (Istanbul): Yeni Cami (pronounced "Yeni New Mosque originally named Valide Sultan Mosque (Turkish "Valide Sultan Camii" ) later New Valide Sultan Mosque (Turkish "Yeni Valide Sultan Camii" ) after partial reconstruction completion between 1660 and 1665; Ottoman imperial mosque in Eminönü quarter of Istanbul, Turkey situated on Golden Horn, southern end of Galata Bridge one of famous architectural landmarks of Istanbul.
 Vasat Atik Ali Pasha Mosque: (Turkish: "Vasat Atik Ali Paşa Camii" also known as Zincirlikuyu Mosque (Turkish: "Zincirlikuyu Camii" ) or Karagümrük Mosque, Ottoman mosque in Karagümrük neighbourhood of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey, on Fevzipaşa Street.Sultan Bayezid II's grand vizier Hadım Atik Ali Pasha, after mosque named ordered construction in 1502 completed in 1512, one year after grand vizier's death.
 Atik Mustafa Pasha Mosque: Atik Mosque (Turkish: "Atik Mustafa Paşa Camii" ; also named "Hazreti Cabir Camii") is former Eastern Orthodox church in Istanbul converted into mosque by Ottomans. dedication church obscure. identified with church of Saints Peter and Mark without proof. Now probable church identified with Saint Thekla of the Palace of Blachernae (Greek: Άγία Θέκλα τοῦ Παλατίου τῶν Βλαχερνών , "Hagia Thekla tou Palatiou tōn Vlakhernōn"). building belongs stylistically to eleventh-twelfth century.

Temple of Music: Temple Music was a concert hall and auditorium built for Pan-American Exposition held in Buffalo, New York in 1901. U.S. President William McKinley assassinated inside building on September 6, 1901. structure, like other buildings at exposition demolished when fair ended.
 Pan-American Exposition: Pan Exposition was World's Fair held in Buffalo, New York, United States, from May 1 through November 2, 1901. fair occupied 350 acre land on western edge of now Delaware Park extending from Delaware Avenue to Elmwood Avenue northward to Great Arrow Avenue. remembered for location of assassination of President William McKinley.
 Assassination of William McKinley: On September 6, 1901 William McKinley, 25th President of United States, was shot on grounds Pan-American Exposition at Temple of Music in Buffalo, New York. shaking hands with public when Leon Czolgosz, anarchist, shot him twice in abdomen. McKinley died eight days later on September 14 of gangrene by gunshot wounds. was third American president to assassinated, following Abraham Lincoln in 1865 James A. Garfield in 1881.
 Alice Russell Glenny: Alice Russell Glenny (1858–1924) was American painter, sculptor, graphic artist lived worked in Buffalo, New York. fixture of artistic scene in Buffalo in early twentieth century. From 1893-1894 and 1903–1904 served as president of Buffalo Society of Artists studied under top teachers William Merritt Chase and Gustav Boulanger in United States and France considered one of city's top artists. Glenny remembered for Art Nouveau posters and magazine illustrations. posters featured in Buffalo's Pan-American Exposition of 1901 famous for location of shooting of President William McKinley.She regularly contributed illustrations to Buffalo-Courier Express, major newspapers in Buffalo.
 Assassination of James A. Garfield: James A. Garfield, 20th President of United States assassinated at 9:30 am on July 2, 1881, less than four months into his term as President. shot by Charles J. Guiteau at Baltimore and Potomac Railroad Station in Washington, D.C. died in Elberon, New Jersey on September 19, 1881. Guiteau's motive was revenge against Garfield for imagined political debt. Garfield second of four Presidents to be assassinated, following Abraham Lincoln preceding William McKinley and John F. Kennedy. His Vice President, Chester A. Arthur, succeeded Garfield as President.
 1901 State of the Union Address: 1901 State of Union Address given Tuesday, December 3, 1901, by 26th President of United States, Theodore Roosevelt. presented to both houses of 57th United States Congress, he was not present. He stated, "The Congress assembles year under shadow of great calamity. sixth of September, President McKinley shot by anarchist while attending Pan-American Exposition at Buffalo died in that city on fourteenth of that month." concluded with "Indeed from every quarter civilized world received President's death, assurances of grief and regard touch hearts people. In affliction we reverently thank the Almighty we at peace with nations of mankind; intend policy to continue unbroken international relations of mutual respect and good will."

Son of Zorn: Son of Zorn is an American live-action/animated sitcom television series created by Reed Agnew and Eli Jorné. aired on Fox from September 11, 2016, to February 19, 2017. series stars Cheryl Hines, Johnny Pemberton, Tim Meadows, Artemis Pebdani, and Jason Sudeikis as the voice of Zorn.
 Johnny Pemberton: Johnny Pemberton (born in 1981) is an American actor and comedian from Rochester, Minnesota. best known for his role as titular "Son of Zorn" in short-lived Fox sitcom, and also appeared as recurring character Bo Thompson in NBC sitcom "Superstore".
 Superstore (TV series): Superstore is an American single-camera sitcom television series premiered on NBC on November 30, 2015. series created by Justin Spitzer, also serves as executive producer. Starring America Ferrera (who also serves as producer) and Ben Feldman, "Superstore" follows group of employees working at "Cloud 9", store number 1217, a fictional big-box store in St. Louis, Missouri. ensemble and supporting cast features Lauren Ash, Colton Dunn, Nico Santos, Nichole Bloom, and Mark McKinney.
 Lea Thompson: Lea Katherine Thompson (born May 31, 1961) is an American actress, television director, and television producer. known for her role as Lorraine Baines in "Back to the Future" trilogy and title character in 1990s NBC sitcom "Caroline in City". Other films for known include "All the Right Moves" (1983), "Red Dawn" (1984), "Howard the Duck" (1986) "Some Kind of Wonderful" (1987), and "The Beverly Hillbillies" (1993). From 2011-2017, co-starred as Kathryn Kennish in Freeform (formerly ABC Family) series "Switched at Birth".
 Bo Brady: Bo Brady is a fictional character on the NBC soap opera, "Days of Our Lives", the youngest of the series' Brady family.Created under head-writer Margaret DePriest, role originated by Peter Reckell on May 3, 1983. Reckell left the show alongside Kristian Alfonso who played Bo's wife Hope Williams Brady on April 20, 1987. Reckell returned from April 19, 1990, to January 17, 1992, when Robert Kelker-Kelly stepped into the role from March 13, 1992, to July 24, 1995. Reckell returned to portray Bo on August 1, 1995. In June 2012, after speculation, confirmed Reckell would once again exit the soap. Reckell filmed final scenes for "Days of our Lives" on July 24, 2012, last airing on October 30. announced on March 18, 2015, Reckell inked a deal to return for show's fiftieth anniversary, airing on August 28, 2015. In May 2016, announced Reckell would return for special episode centered around Hope, airing on June 7 and 8, 2016.
 Fred G. Sanford: Fred G. Sanford is a fictional character portrayed by actor/comedian Redd Foxx on 1972–1977 NBC sitcom "Sanford and Son" and 1980–1981 NBC sitcom "Sanford".
 Nick Zano: Nick Zano (born March 8, 1978) is an American actor and producer. best known for played Vince in The WB's sitcom "What I Like About You". got big break on MTV, hosted network's former infotainment program about the film industry, "Movie House", and briefly worked as an MTV News correspondent before began acting career. recurring roles on television include Drew Pragin on "Melrose Place", Josh on "Cougar Town", Pete on "Happy Endings", P.J. Hillingsbrook on "90210", and Johnny on "2 Broke Girls". He also starred as a lead on NBC sitcom "One Big Happy" and as Arthur in the TV series "Minority Report". He currently stars as Dr. Nate Heywood/Steel on The CW show "Legends of Tomorrow".

 The Fish Can Sing: (Icelandic "Brekkukotsannáll" ) 1957 novel by Icelandic author Halldór Laxness awarded Nobel Prize in Literature 1955.
 Independent People: Independent (Icelandic "Sjálfstætt fólk" ) epic novel by Nobel laureate Halldór Laxness published in two volumes 1934 and 1935 title means "Self-standing self-reliant] folk". deals with struggle of poor Icelandic farmers early 20th century freed from debt bondage last generation surviving on isolated crofts inhospitable landscape.
 Memoir of Halldór Laxness: Memoir Laxness published in Iceland from 2003. memoir of novelist Nobel Laureate Halldór Laxnessf in three volumes:
 Guðný Halldórsdóttir: Guðný Halldórsdóttir (born 23 January 1954) Icelandic film director screenwriter directed eight films since 1984 2007 film "The Quiet Storm" entered 30th Moscow International Film Festival. father was writer 1955 Nobel prize winner Halldór Laxness mother writer textile designer Auður Laxness.
 Auður Laxness: Auður Sveinsdóttir Laxness (1918-2012) Icelandic writer craftswoman influencing design popularity of Icelandic Lopapeysa sweater mid-20th century husband was Icelandic Nobel Literature laureate Halldór Laxness Auður worked as his secretary writing collaborator.
 Einar Arnórsson: Einar Arnórsson (24 February 1880 – 29 March 1955) was Minister for Iceland from 4 May 1915 to 4 January 1917. graduated in Law from University of Copenhagen 1906. elected to Althingi sat there 1914–1919 and 1931–1932 for Independence party.Minister of Education and Justice in Björn Þórðarson's cabinet from 1942 to 1944. professor of Law at University of Iceland from 1911 to 1915 after leaving office Minister for Iceland from 1917 to 1922. Supreme Court Judge in 1932–1942 1944–1945. president of University of Iceland in 1918–1919 1929–1930. short time father-in-law to Halldór Laxness. editor of "Ísafold" and "Morgunblaðið" in 1919–1920.

Ex parte Endo: or Mitsuye Endo, 323 U.S. 283 (1944), was United States Supreme Court ex parte decision December 18, 1944 Justices unanimously ruled U.S. government could not continue detain citizen "concededly loyal" to United States. Court not touch on constitutionality of exclusion of Japanese ancestry from West Coast—which found not violate citizen rights in "Korematsu v. United States" decision same Endo ruling led to reopening of West Coast to Japanese Americans after incarceration in camps U.S. interior during World War II.
 Dale Minami: (born October 13, 1946) is San Francisco-based lawyer known for heading legal team overturned conviction of Fred Korematsu, defiance of World War II Japanese American internment order lead to Korematsu v. United States, one of most controversial United States Supreme Court decisions of 20th century.
 Eric Yamamoto: Yamamoto, Korematsu Professor of Law and Social Justice at University of Hawaiʻ i at Mānoa William S. Richardson School of Law, internationally recognized expert on issues racial justice including racial reconciliation and redress. landmark Korematsu v. United States case known for work as member of Fred Korematsu's legal team.
 UC Berkeley School of Law: University of California, Berkeley, School of Law, referred Berkeley Law and Boalt Hall, one of 14 schools and colleges at University of California, Berkeley. Berkeley Law ranked as one of top law schools in nation.law school produced leaders in law, government society, including Chief Justice States Earl Warren, Secretary of State Dean Rusk Attorney General States Edwin Meese States Secretary of Treasury Chairman of Federal Reserve G. William Miller, Solicitor General United States Theodore Olson lead litigator of "Korematsu v. United States" civil rights case, Dale Minami.
 Duncan v. Kahanamoku: Duncan v., 327 U.S. 304 (1946), decision by United States Supreme Court. associated with Japanese exclusion cases ("Hirabayashi v. United States", "Korematsu v. United States" "Ex parte Endo") because involved wartime curtailment of fundamental civil liberties under military authority this case neither plaintiff nor nominal defendant were Japanese.
 Korematsu v. United States: v, 323 U.S. 214 (1944) landmark United States Supreme Court case concerning constitutionality of Executive Order 9066, ordered Japanese Americans into internment camps during World War II regardless of citizenship.
 Chaplinsky v. New Hampshire: Chaplinsky v, 315 U.S. 568 (1942), United States Supreme Court case Court articulated fighting words doctrine, limitation of First Amendment's guarantee of freedom of speech.
 Freedom of movement under United States law: governed by Privileges and Immunities Clause of United States Constitution states "The Citizens of each State entitled to all Privileges and Immunities of Citizens in several States." circuit court ruling in "Corfield v. Coryell," 6 Fed. Cas. 546 (1823), freedom of movement judicially recognized as fundamental Constitutional right. In "Paul v. Virginia," 75 U.S.168 (1869) Court defined freedom of movement as "right of free ingress into other States egress from them." Supreme Court invest federal government with authority to protect freedom of movement Under "privileges and immunities" clause authority given to states position Court held consistently in cases "Ward v. Maryland, 79 U.S. 418 (1871) "Slaughter-House Cases, 83 U.S. 36 (1873) "United States v. Harris, 106 U.S. 629 (1883).

Katharine Graham: Katharine Meyer Graham (June 16, 1917 – July 17, 2001) was an American publisher. She led her family's newspaper, "The Washington Post", for more than two decades, overseeing its most famous period, the Watergate coverage that eventually led to the resignation of President Richard Nixon. Her memoir, "Personal History", won the Pulitzer Prize in 1998.
 Black and White Ball: The Black and White Ball was a masquerade ball held on November 28, 1966 at the Plaza Hotel in New York City. Hosted by author Truman Capote, ball was in honor of "The Washington Post" publisher Katharine Graham.
 Common iora: The common iora ("Aegithina tiphia") is a small passerine bird found across the tropical Indian subcontinent with populations showing plumage variations, some of are designated as subspecies. A species found in scrub and forest, it is easily detected from its loud whistles and bright colours. During the breeding season, males display by fluffing up their feathers and spiral in the air appearing like a green, black, yellow and white ball.
 Blackballing: Blackballing is a rejection in a traditional form of secret ballot, where a white ball or ballot constitutes a vote in support and a black ball signifies opposition. This system is typically used where a club's rules provide that one or two objections, rather than an at-least-50% share of votes, are sufficient to defeat a proposition. Since the seventeenth century, these rules have commonly applied to elections to membership of many gentlemen's clubs and similar institutions such as Freemasonry and fraternities.
 Sight screen: The function of the sight screen, is usually completely black or white in color, is to offer batsman a clean view of the bowler and his or her delivery, such that distractions including spectators do not disturb the batsman. In limited overs matches such as One Day Internationals or Twenty20 Internationals, usually played with a white ball, the sight screen is usually black, or otherwise dark.In Test matches, in a cherry-red ball is used for play, the sight screen is usually white.

Huis Ten Bosch (theme park): Huis Ten Bosch (ハウステンボス , "Hausu Ten Bosu" ) is a theme park in Sasebo, Nagasaki, Japan, recreates the Netherlands by displaying life-sized copies of old Dutch buildings. name Huis Ten Bosch translates into English as "House in the Woods/bush". named after Huis ten Bosch, one of three official residences of Dutch Royal Family, located in The Hague in Netherlands and former home to Princess Beatrix.
 Huis Ten Bosch Station: Huis Ten Bosch Station (ハウステンボス駅 , Hausutenbosu-eki ) is a railway station on the Ōmura Line in Haenosaki-chō, Sasebo, Nagasaki Prefecture, Japan operated by Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu).
 Huis Ten Bosch (train): Huis Ten Bosch (ハウステンボス , Hausutenbosu ) is a limited express train service operated by Kyushu Railway Company (JR Kyushu) in Japan. runs between Hakata Station in Fukuoka, Fukuoka, and Huis Ten Bosch Station, station for Huis Ten Bosch theme park in Sasebo, Nagasaki.
 Huis ten Bosch palace: Huis ten Bosch (] ; English: "House in the Woods") is a royal palace in The Hague in Netherlands. one of three official residences of Dutch Royal Family, the other two being Noordeinde Palace in The Hague and Royal Palace in Amsterdam.
 Huis ten Bosch (disambiguation): Huis ten Bosch is a Royal palace in The Hague, Netherlands and former home of Queen Beatrix of The Netherlands.
 Oranjezaal: The Oranjezaal refers to a painted ballroom in Royal palace Huis ten Bosch in the Hague. It was once, together with neighboring "Chinese room", part of first national museum of the Netherlands founded in 1800 called the "Nationale Konst-Gallery". supervisor Cornelis Sebille Roos appointed Jan Gerard Waldorp as first custodian and curator to receive visitors (for 6 stuivers) and explain collection.

Clement Attlee: Clement Richard Attlee, 1st Earl Attlee, {'1': ", '2': ", '3': ", '4': "} (3 January 1883 – 8 October 1967) was a British Labour politician who served as Prime Minister of United Kingdom from 1945 to 1951 and Leader of the Labour Party from 1935 to 1955. In 1940, Attlee took Labour into the wartime coalition government and served under Winston Churchill, becoming the first person to hold the office of Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom. He on to lead the Labour Party to unexpected landslide victory at 1945 general election; forming first Labour majority government, and a mandate to implement its postwar reforms. The 12.0% national swing from the Conservatives to Labour was unprecedented at that time and remains the largest ever achieved by any party at a general election in British electoral history. He was re-elected with a narrow majority at 1950 general election. In the following year, Attlee called a snap general election, hoping to increase his parliamentary majority. However, he was narrowly defeated by Conservatives under leadership of Winston Churchill; despite winning the most votes of any political party in any general election in British political history until Conservative Party's fourth consecutive victory in 1992. Attlee remains the longest-ever serving Leader of the Labour Party.
 Distribution of Industry Act 1950: The Distribution of Industry Act 1950 was an Act of Parliament passed in the United Kingdom by the Labour government of Clement Attlee. It strengthened the powers of Board of Trade in the Development Areas, making “further provision for acquisition of land, creation of easements and carrying out of work in development areas.” It also authorized “the Board of Trade “to make grants, in exceptional cases in connection with establishment in, or transfer to, development areas of industrial undertakings, and to make grants or loans to housing associations for the provision of dwellings in development areas.” In addition, the Act also provided for payments towards the cost of removal and resettlement of key workers and their dependants.
Gordon Bajnai: György Gordon Bajnai (] ; born 5 March 1968) is a Hungarian entrepreneur and economist, served as the seventh Prime Minister of Hungary from 2009 to 2010. In March 2009, following Prime Minister Ferenc Gyurcsány's announced resignation, Bajnai was nominated by the ruling Hungarian Socialist Party (MSZP) to become Hungary's next prime minister. Bajnai became prime minister when parliament passed a constructive motion of no-confidence against Ferenc Gyurcsány on 14 April 2009.
 Industry Act 1975: The Industry Act 1975 (c. 68) was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom passed by Harold Wilson's Labour government.
 Honours (Prevention of Abuses) Act 1925: The Honours (Prevention of Abuses) Act 1925 is an Act of Parliament of United Kingdom, makes the sale of peerages or any other honours illegal. It was brought in after the Coalition government of David Lloyd George was severely embarrassed by the sale of honours, for personal financial gain of Prime Minister. The practice was legal and dated back several decades, Lloyd George made practice more systematic and more brazen, charging £10,000 for a knighthood, £30,000 for baronetcy, and £50,000 upwards for a peerage. Prime Minister Lloyd George in mid-1922 was fast losing his political support, and his sales were denounced in the House of Lords as an abuse of the Prime Minister's powers of patronage.

Ghosts (2006 film): Ghosts is a 2006 drama film directed by Nick Broomfield based on 2004 Morecambe Bay cockling disaster. title is reference to Cantonese slang term "Gweilo" (鬼佬), meaning "ghost man", used for white people.
 Cantonese slang: Cantonese slang is type slang used in areas where Cantonese language spoken.
 Gweilo: Gweilo or gwailou ( pronounced ] ) is common Cantonese slang term for Westerners. unmodified form applies only to European ethnicities history of racially deprecatory use. Cantonese speakers frequently use "gwailou" to refer to Westerners in general use in non-derogatory context, whether usage offensive disputed by Cantonese and Westerners.
 Beard (companion): Beard is slang term describing person used knowingly or unknowingly, as date, romantic partner (boyfriend or girlfriend), or spouse to conceal infidelity or conceal sexual orientation. American slang term originally referred to anyone who acted on behalf of another in transaction to conceal person's true identity. term used in heterosexual and homosexual contexts especially used within LGBT culture. References to beards seen in mainstream television and films, other entertainment.
 Shiv (weapon): Shiv (possibly from Romani word "chivomengro", "knife"), also "chiv", is slang term for any sharp or pointed implement used as knife-like weapon. "Oxford English Dictionary" suggests "shive", a razor, documented in 1915, as root word. In 1920s, "shiv" was also common slang term for bladed weapon, mostly knife. In United States, improvised prison knife also often called a shank.
 Dongo: Dongo may refer to mix between dingo and any other dog referred to as "Dongo" and slang term for male genitalia.Dongo reported to be not widely used, as slang term in Australia substitute for color orange.
 Ducking (slang): "Ducking" is a prison slang term for technique prisoners modify behavior of correctional officers other prison staff members using manipulation and coercion. prison slang term for prison staff member manipulated is a "duck".
 Shmohawk: Shmohawk or schmohawk is slang term might have derived from "schmo", slang term meaning "fool". HBO television show "Curb Your Enthusiasm" gave word recent notoriety, HBO sells a "Curb Your Enthusiasm" schmohawk mug Earlier uses of word found in "Crusader Rabbit" animated cartoon "Crusader and the Schmohawk Indians", released in 1950 and in Saul Bellow's 1958 novel "Henderson the Rain King".

Tian Tan Buddha: also known as Big Buddha, is large bronze statue of Buddha Shakyamuni completed in 1993 located at Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, in Hong Kong statue near Po Lin Monastery symbolises harmonious relationship between man and nature, people faith major centre of Buddhism in Hong Kong popular tourist attraction.
 Po Lin Monastery: is Buddhist monastery located on Ngong Ping Plateau, Lantau Island, Hong Kong.
 Buddhism in Hong Kong: Buddhism major religion in Hong Kong influential in traditional culture populace. prominent Buddhist temples Chi Lin Nunnery in Diamond Hill built in Tang Dynasty's architectural style; Po Lin Monastery on Lantau Island famous for outdoor bronze statue, Tian Tan Buddha attracts large visitors during weekends and holidays
 Nei Lak Shan: (Chinese: 彌勒山) is sixth highest hill in Hong Kong height of 751 m on Lantau Island north of Ngong Ping where Buddhist Po Lin Monastery. "Nei Lak", "Mei Lak" is Cantonese language translation of Maitreya, future Buddha, in Buddhism.
