 Ngong Ping 360: Ngong Ping 360 is gondola lift on Lantau Island in Hong Kong to improve tourism lift previously known as Tung Chung Cable Car Project before Ngong Ping 360 brand in April 2005. consists of Ngong Ping Cable Car, formerly known as Ngong Ping 360 Skyrail, and Ngong Ping Village, retail and entertainment centre adjacent to cable car's upper station. Ngong Ping 360 connects Tung Chung, north coast of Lantau linked to central Hong Kong by Tung Chung Line with Ngong Ping area in hills abovehome to Po Lin Monastery Tian Tan Buddha, both significant tourist attractions. Before Ngong Ping 360's opening only access was via mountain road bus service.
 Ngong Ping: Ngong Ping () is a highland in western part of Lantau Island, Hong Kong hosts Po Lin Monastery Tian Tan Buddha amidst hills about 34 m tall. several hills nearby attraction to tourists now terminus of cable car ride Ngong Ping 360 travels to Tung Chung. New facilities tourist attractions opened including Ngong Ping Village, Walking with the Buddha, Monkey's Tale Theatre Ngong Ping Tea House. youth hostel located near monastery. second highest peak of Hong Kong, Lantau Peak, at southeast.
 Enchey Monastery: established in 1909 above Gangtok, capital city of Sikkim Northeastern Indian state belongs to Nyingma order of Vajrayana Buddhism monastery built around small hamlet Gangtok became religious centre location blessed by Lama Drupthob Karpo, renowned exponent of tantric (adept) art in Buddhism with flying powers initially small Gompa established by him after flew from Maenam Hill in South Sikkim to site literal meaning of Enchey Monastery is "Solitary Monastery". sacredness attributed to belief Khangchendzonga and Yabdean – protecting deities – reside in monastery according to legend Guru Padmasambhava subdued spirits of Khangchendzonga, Yabdean Mahākāla here legend religious significance of Enchey Monastery deeply ingrained in every household in Gangtok believed powerful deities fulfil wishes of devotees.

Dirk Nowitzki: Dirk Werner Nowitzki (] ) (born June 19, 1978) is a German professional basketball player for Dallas Mavericks of National Basketball Association (NBA). alumnus of Röntgen Gymnasium and DJK Würzburg basketball club, Nowitzki was chosen as ninth pick in 1998 NBA draft by Milwaukee Bucks immediately traded to Mavericks, where played since. Listed at 7 ft , Nowitzki is considered to be one of the greatest power forwards of all time.
 Austin Rivers: Austin James Rivers (born August 1, 1992) is an American professional basketball player for Los Angeles Clippers of National Basketball Association (NBA). Rivers led Winter Park High School to back-to-back Florida 6A state championships in 2010 and 2011. also played in 2011 Nike Hoop Summit for Team USA, and was a McDonald's All-American. He was one of top rated high school basketball players in class of 2011, rated as high as No. 1 by Rivals.com. On September 30, 2010, Rivers committed to Duke University. Rivers gained national recognition after making a game winning 3-pointer against Duke rival North Carolina in 2012. drafted with 10th pick in NBA draft by New Orleans Hornets (now Pelicans), playing three seasons there before traded to Clippers.
 Terrance Ferguson: Terrance Eugene Ferguson (born May 17, 1998) is an American professional basketball player for Oklahoma City Thunder of National Basketball Association (NBA). completed high school at Advanced Preparatory International in Dallas, Texas, was a top-20 player in Class of 2016. Ferguson made separate commitments to both Alabama and Arizona before deciding to skip college and play overseas in 2016–17. Ferguson is three-time gold medalist with Team USA, in 2016, participated in McDonald's All-American Game and Nike Hoop Summit, winning MVP award at the latter.
Tyus Jones: Tyus Robert Jones (born May 10, 1996) is an American professional basketball player for Minnesota Timberwolves of National Basketball Association (NBA). played college basketball for Duke Blue Devils in freshman season part of 2014–15 National Championship team. ranked among top 10 players in the national high school class of 2014 by Rivals.com, Scout.com and ESPN. was a Minnesota State High School League (MSHSL) Class 4A state champion, three-time Minnesota Associated Press Boys Basketball Player of the Year and three-time Minnesota Boys Basketball Gatorade Player of the Year for Apple Valley High School. played in the 2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game, 2014 Jordan Brand Classic and 2014 Nike Hoop Summit. won skills competition at 2014 McDonald's All-American Game and posted only double-double in 2014 Jordan Brand Classic.
 Keijuro Matsui: Keijuro Matsui (popularly known as KJ) (born October 16, 1985) was a guard for Columbia Lions basketball team at Columbia University. is first Japanese native basketball player in NCAA Division I history. Matsui played in 2005 Nike Hoop Summit for World Select Team, only second Japanese to do so. In summit scored seven points in 11 minutes.
 Nike Hoop Summit: Nike Hoop Summit is an international men's basketball all-star game sponsored by Nike, held once a year since 1995, features the USA Basketball Men's Junior Select Team against World Select Team of international players. players demonstrate skills and hope to attract attention from NBA scouts or colleges. A of current NBA players have participated in this event in the past, including Kevin Garnett, Derrick Rose, Kevin Durant, John Wall for U.S.A. team, and Dirk Nowitzki, Tony Parker, Nicolas Batum, Serge Ibaka, Enes Kanter, and Patrick Mills for World Select team.2010 edition event, Enes Kanter scored 34 points surpassed event's record of 33 points set by Dirk Nowitzki in 1998. Bismack Biyombo recorded first triple-double in Hoop Summit history in 2011 with 12 points, 11 rebounds, 10 blocks. In 2012, Shabazz Muhammad scored 35 points to break Enes Kanter's Hoop Summit scoring record.

Final Recipe: Final Recipe is a 2013 South Korean-Thai drama film directed by Gina Kim written by George Huang, adapted a story by Kim. stars Michelle Yeoh, Henry Lau, and Chin Han. Lau plays a young man who must impress host of cooking show (Yeoh) and her chef husband (Han) to save his grandfather's restaurant. premiered at San Sebastián International Film Festival.
 Henry Lau: Henry Lau (born October 11, 1989), known mononymously as Henry, is a Canadian singer, rapper, dancer, composer, record producer, beatboxer, actor and entertainer mostly active in South Korea. debuted in 2008 as a member of Super Junior-M. Aside from group activities, has also produce several songs for various artists, television drama and a part of composing team NoizeBank. dubbed his fans as his Strings.
 Cho Kyu-hyun discography: Cho Kyuhyun (better known by his mononym Kyuhyun) is a South Korean singer. His discography consists of one studio album, three extended plays, seven singles, three promotional singles, seventeen soundtrack songs. debuted as a member of South Korean boy band Super Junior in 2006 subsequently became a part of its subgroup Super Junior-K.R.Y. in 2006 and Super Junior-M in 2008 S.M. Entertainment's group SM the Ballad in 2010.
 Cho Kyuhyun: Cho Kyu-hyun (born February 3, 1988), better known mononymously as Kyuhyun, is a South Korean singer and musical theatre actor. best known as a member of South Korean boy group Super Junior, its sub-groups Super Junior-K.R.Y., Super Junior-M and former member of South Korean ballad group S.M. the Ballad. one of first four Korean artists to appear on Chinese postage stamps.
 Lee Donghae: Lee Dong-hae (hangul: 이동해; hanja: 李東海; born October 15, 1986) is a South Korean singer, songwriter and actor.He is a member of boy band Super Junior, its subgroup Super Junior-M, and Super Junior-D&E, well as dance-centered group SM The Performance. He is one of first four Korean artists to appear on Chinese postage stamps.
 Lee Sung-min (singer): Lee Sung-min (born January 1, 1986) is a South Korean singer and actor. He a member of South Korean boy band Super Junior and sub-groups Super Junior-T, Super Junior-H and Super Junior-M.

Pieris (plant): Pieris ( or ) is a genus of seven species of shrubs in family Ericaceae, native to mountain regions of eastern and southern Asia, eastern North America Cuba. Known commonly in North America as andromedas or fetterbushes, they are broad-leaved evergreen shrubs growing to 1 - tall and 3 - wide. leaves are spirally arranged, often appearing to in whorls at end of each shoot with bare stretches of shoot below; are lanceolate-ovate, 2 - long and 1.0 - broad, leathery textured, with entire or serrated margin. young leaves in spring are typically brightly coloured. flowers are bell-shaped, 5 - long, white or pink, arranged in racemes 5 - long. fruit is a woody capsule splits into five sections to release numerous small seeds.
 Pieris (butterfly): Pieris, the whites or garden whites, is a widespread now almost cosmopolitan genus of butterflies of family Pieridae. highest species diversity is in Palearctic. Many species of genus have caterpillars feed on cabbage and other members of Brassicaceae. chemical basis of association with certain plant group studied for over 100 years, now known to occur via biochemical adaptations to chemicals called glucosinolates in these plants. In contrast to other insects, "Pieris" caterpillars to detoxify these chemicals specialised they will not eat food without glucosinolates. "Pieris" females check for presence of glucosinolates before laying eggs on plant. crop-damaging species spread from Eurasia to most rest of world (most recently to South America and Africa) are considered pest insects almost everywhere. are species of "Pieris" are not pests, such as North American species "Pieris oleracea" and "Pieris virginiensis". These butterflies feed only on specific native vegetation.
Phlebodium: Phlebodium is a small genus of two to four species of ferns, native to tropical and subtropical regions of Americas. genus closely related to "Polypodium", species were formerly included in that genus.
 Phlebodium aureum: Phlebodium aureum (golden polypody, golden serpent fern, cabbage palm fern, gold-foot fern, hare-foot fern; syn. "Polypodium aureum", "Polypodium leucatomos") is an epiphytic fern native to tropical and subtropical regions of Americas. confined to eastern side of continents, extending north into United States to Florida and extreme southeast of Georgia, south through Caribbean (the Bahamas, Puerto Rico, Lesser Antilles), northern and eastern South America to Paraguay. only species of "Phlebodium" found in North America, other species all confined to South America. Other common names include calaguala (Spanish language), laua`e haole (Hawaiian), samambaia (Portuguese), hartassbräken (Swedish).
 Pieris floribunda: Pieris floribunda is North American species of broadleaf evergreen shrub, member of fetterbush genus in blueberry family (Ericaceae). commonly known in North America as mountain fetterbush or mountain andromeda. All parts of "Pieris floribunda" are poisonous if ingested rare plant to find in landscapes difficult to propagate often does not adapt well to cultivation, few specialty and native plant nurseries sell some, overcoming difficult propagation. In landscapes should be grown in full to part shade, out of windy locations, have good quality soil with lots of organic matter acid of pH 4.5 to 6.5

Franklin Seaver Pratt: Franklin Seaver Pratt (November 1, 1829 – January 11, 1894), also known as Franklyn or Frank S. Pratt, was American settler, businessman, public servant diplomat of Kingdom of Hawaii. married Elizabeth Kekaʻaniau Laʻanui, member Hawaiian nobility, defended her claims to Hawaiian crown lands during overthrow of Kingdom of Hawaii.
 Thomas Howard, 2nd Duke of Norfolk: Thomas Howard, 2nd Duke of Norfolk (1443 – 21 May 1524), styled Earl of Surrey from 1483 to 1485 and again from 1489 to 1514, was English nobleman politician. only son of John Howard, 1st Duke of Norfolk, by first wife, Katherine Moleyns. Duke grandfather of Queen Anne Boleyn and Queen Catherine Howard great grandfather of Queen Elizabeth I. served four monarchs as soldier and statesman.
 Elizabeth Kekaaniau: Elizabeth Kekaʻaniau Laʻanui Pratt, full name Elizabeth Kekaikuihala Kekaʻaniauokalani Kalaninuiohilaukapu Laʻanui Pratt (12 September 1834 – 20 December 1928) was great grandniece of Kamehameha I great granddaughter of Kalokuokamaile, older brother of Kamehameha I, founder of Kingdom of Hawaii.
 Nigel Loring (surgeon): Sir John Nigel Loring {} (1896–1979) was Apothecary to British Royalty. son of Nele and Mabel Alice (Isaac) Loring born 31 August 1896 seventh great grandson to New England immigrant Thomas Loring. great great grandfather Joshua Loring United Empire Loyalist from great great grandfather's generation branch of family returned to British Isles.
Al Fakhro: Al-Fakhroh Tribe , (Arabic: آل فخروه ; also spelled Al-Fakhroo) attributing to great grandfather Fakher from Banu Tamim. name Fakhroh came from great grandfather Fakher son of Tamim bin Mor bin Ad bin Muder bin Adnan considered ancient Arab tribe dwelled by people from Arabian Peninsula.
 Death and state funeral of Gerald Ford: December 26, 2006, Gerald Ford, 38th President of United States, died at home in Rancho Mirage, California at 6:45 p.m. local time (02:45, December 27, UTC). 8:49 p.m. local time President Ford's wife of 58 years, Betty Ford, issued statement confirmed his death: "My family joins in sharing difficult news Gerald Ford, our beloved husband, father, grandfather and great grandfather died at 93 years of age. His life was filled with love of God, family and country." causes of death on death certificate were arteriosclerotic cerebrovascular disease and cardiac arrest.
 Teispes: Teïspes (from Greek Τεΐσπης ; in Old Persian: "Cišpiš") ruled <a href="Anshan%20%28Persia%29">Anshann 675–640 BCE. son of Achaemenes of Persis ancestor of Cyrus the Great. evidence Cyrus I and Ariaramnes were both his sons. Cyrus I grandfather of Cyrus the Great Ariaramnes great grandfather of Darius the Great. to 7th-century BC documents he captured Elamite city of Anshan, speculated after Persians freed from Median supremacy, expanded his small kingdom. kingdom was vassal state of Neo Assyrian Empire (911–605 BCE). succeeded by second son, Cyrus I.

Mille Lune Mille Onde: "Mille Lune Mille Onde" is second single from Italian pop tenor Andrea Bocelli's 2001 album, "Cieli di Toscana". song written by Francesco Sartori, Claudio Corradini Lucio Quarantotto, writers of Bocelli's "Con te partirò" and "Canto della Terra", and by multiple Grammy Award winner David Foster, among Bocelli's most popular well-known songs. song used in Barilla's pasta commercials.
 Melodramma (song): "Melodramma" is lead single from Italian pop tenor Andrea Bocelli's 2001 album, "Cieli di Toscana". song written by Pierpaolo Guerrini and Paolo Luciani among Bocelli's most popular well-known songs.
 Cieli di Toscana: Cieli di Toscana (Tuscan Skies) is Andrea Bocelli's eighth studio album, released in 2001.
 Tuscan Skies: Tuscan Skies (Cieli di Toscana) is third DVD released by Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli.
 Andrea Bocelli: Andrea Bocelli, (] ; born 22 September 1958) is Italian classical crossover tenor, recording artist, singer-songwriter. Born with poor eyesight, Bocelli became completely blind at age of 12, following football accident.
 Ferdinand IV, Grand Duke of Tuscany: Ferdinand IV, Grand Duke of Tuscany (Italian: "Ferdinando IV, Granduca di Toscana" ; 10 June 1835 – 17 January 1908) was last Grand Duke of Tuscany from 1859 to 1860. House of Habsburg-Lorraine continued to hold title as pretenders until end of World War I.
 Ottaviano de' Medici (b. 1957): Prince Ottaviano de' Medici Ottaviano di Toscana aka Ottaviano de' Medici di Toscana di Ottajano (b. 1957) is Italian noble member of Ottajano branch of House of Medici. president of Associazione Internationale Medicae (International Medici Association) one of founders of Save Florence, initiative to conserve cultural heritage of city of.

Naomi Campbell: Naomi Elaine Campbell (born 22 May 1970) is English model and actress. Recruited at age of 15 established herself among top three most recognisable in-demand models of late 1980s and 1990s, one of six models of her generation declared :supermodels by fashion industry.
 Nasty Girl (The Notorious B.I.G. song): "Nasty Girl" is song by rapper The Notorious B.I.G. released in 2005 in US and January 16, 2006 in UK. single reached #1 in United Kingdom (this his first #1 in the country, under a year after "rival" rapper 2Pac achieved first #1 with "Ghetto Gospel"). song features guest appearances from Jagged Edge, P. Diddy, Avery Storm, Nelly video contains guest appearances from Pharrell, Usher, Fat Joe, 8 Ball & MJG, Teairra Mari, Jazze Pha, DJ Green Lantern, Naomi Campbell Memphis Bleek found on album "", a remixed album of Biggie Smalls' work. lyrical section rapped by Notorious B.I.G lifted from another his songs "Nasty Boy", featured on his second album "Life After Death". Despite, production to song "Nasty Boy" different from for "Nasty Girl", apart from lyrical sample, second verse (rapped by P. Diddy) rapped in style of Biggie's second verse of Nasty Boy, two songs bear no similarities. chorus, sung by Jagged Edge, line "Grab your titties for B.I.G.", references "Player's Anthem", says "Bitches, rub your titties if you love Big Poppa".
 Duets: The Final Chapter: Duets: The Final Chapter (sometimes referred as The Biggie Duets) is fourth studio album and second and final posthumous album by late American rapper The Notorious B.I.G., collection of songs featuring appearances of other prominent rappers. album released by Bad Boy Records and Atlantic Records on December 20, 2005 charted at #3 selling 438,000 copies, beaten by high sales of Jamie Foxx's "Unpredictable" and Mary J. Blige's "The Breakthrough". In UK climbed high as #13 after release of album's first single "Nasty Girl". his third posthumous album went Double-platinum said to his last album of mainly new material.
 Vanity (singer): Denise Katrina Matthews (January 4, 1959 – February 15, 2016), better known as Vanity, was Canadian singer, songwriter, dancer, actress and model, turned away from music and acting career to concentrate on evangelism. career lasted from early 1980s until mid-1990s. lead singer of female trio Vanity 6 from 1981 until disbanded in 1983. known for 1982 R&B/funk hit "Nasty Girl". Vanity's music career included two solo albums on Motown Records label, "Wild Animal" and "Skin on Skin", minor hit singles "Pretty Mess", "Mechanical Emotion", "Undress" (from movie "Action Jackson"), "Under the Influence". had successful film career, starring in movies "The Last Dragon", "52 Pick-Up", and "Action Jackson". Throughout 1980s to 1990s, Vanity appeared in many magazines. died on February 15, 2016, at age of 57, due to renal failure.
 Total (group): Total is American contemporary R&B girl group one of signature acts of Sean Combs' Bad Boy Records imprint during 1990s. group consisted of members Kima Raynor, Keisha Spivey, and Pamela Long. Total best known for hits "What You Want" (Featuring Mase), "Kissing You", "Can't You See" (featuring The Notorious B.I.G.), "What About Us?" and "Trippin'", both featuring Missy Elliott. Long featured on The Notorious B.I.G.'s hit song "Hypnotize", singing chorus.
 Patrick Kelly (fashion designer): Patrick Kelly (September 24, 1954 – January 1, 1990) was American fashion designer. Born in Vicksburg, Mississippi, Kelly studied art at Jackson State University attended Parsons School of Design. in New York Kelly Struggled to find steady employment. support himself had many jobs included part time job at Baskin Robbins sell his own designs. After receiving advice from friend super model Pat Cleveland anonymous one-way ticket moved to Paris in 1979. Kelly hired as costume designer for nightclub Le Palace. In small apartment shared with model continued to sell his own creations homemade chicken dinners to make ends meet. living in Atlanta at age 18 Kelly sold reworked, recycled clothes served as unpaid window-dresser at Yves Saint Laurent. YSL chairman Pierre Bergé sponsored Kelly in 1988 to form Paris-based womenswear fashion house Patrick Kelly Paris. Kelly achieved greatest commercial success in late 1980s in 1988 Kelly became first American and first person of color to be admitted as member of Chambre syndicale du prêt-à-porter des couturiers et des créateurs de mode. Kelly died at age 35 on New Year's Day, 1990. Originally Kelly's causes of death reported to be bone marrow disease brain tumor, but actual cause of death now acknowledged to be complications of AIDS.

Diana Quick: Diana Marilyn Quick (born 23 November 1946) is an English actress.
 Revengers Tragedy: Revengers Tragedy is a film adaptation of 1606 play "The Revenger's Tragedy" (attributed to Thomas Middleton in credits, following current scholarly consensus). directed by Alex Cox and adapted for screen by Cox's fellow Liverpudlian, Frank Cottrell Boyce. film stars Christopher Eccleston as revenge-obsessed Vindice, with Derek Jacobi as evil Duke, Eddie Izzard as his lecherous son Lussurioso, Diana Quick as the Duchess, Andrew Schofield as Vindice's brother Carlo (a version of play's Hippolito), Carla Henry as his virtuous sister Castiza, and Marc Warren and Justin Salinger as Duchess's sons Supervacuo and Ambitioso.
 Searchers 2.0: Searchers 2.0 is a 2007 road film directed by Alex Cox. stars Del Zamora and Ed Pansullo. Described by Cox as a "microfeature," shot on digital video in 10 days for budget of $180,000. Lacking distribution, featured limited theatrical run of one-night showings at various theaters throughout 2007 and 2008, followed by premier on BBC in UK, and eventual DVD release in Japan and North America. a significant movie in Cox's career as marks his first comedy and first feature-length original screenplay to be produced since "Straight to Hell", 20 years prior.
 Repo Chick: Repo Chick is a 2009 American comedy film written and directed by Alex Cox. Like Cox's first feature, "Repo Man", centers on repossession trade and mysterious vehicle with large reward. second of Cox's "microfeatures", produced for very low budget and given little theatrical distribution. not a sequel to "Repo Man", associated with it. released on DVD in North America and United Kingdom in February 2011.
Antony and Cleopatra (1974 TV drama): Antony and Cleopatra is a 1974 British videotaped television production of William Shakespeare's 1606 play same name, produced by ATV (which distributed internationally by ITC) starring Richard Johnson as Mark Antony, Janet Suzman as Cleopatra, Patrick Stewart as Enobarbus. directed by Jon Scoffield adaptation of Trevor Nunn's Royal Shakespeare Company (RSC) production of play. features-little-known Ben Kingsley and Tim Pigott-Smith in small roles.

Mike Valerio: Mike Valerio is award-winning writer, producer, director executive in entertainment industry for over 20 years. Valerio worked on over a hundred TV shows, films, documentaries mini-series over a dozen television networks entertainment companies. Valerio famous for 1999 film "Carlo's Wake".
 Josh Trank: Joshua Benjamin "Josh" Trank (born February 19, 1984) is American film director, screenwriter editor known for directing 2012 science fiction film "Chronicle" and 2015 superhero film "Fantastic Four", both feature Michael B. Jordan in starring role.
 Fantastic Four (2015 film): Fantastic Four (stylized as Fant4stic) is 2015 American superhero film based on Marvel Comics superhero team of same name. third theatrical "Fantastic Four" film produced distributed by 20th Century Fox reboot of "Fantastic Four" film franchise. Directed by Josh Trank co-wrote screenplay with Jeremy Slater Simon Kinberg, film stars Miles Teller, Michael B. Jordan, Kate Mara Jamie Bell Toby Kebbell. In "Fantastic Four", team must learn to harness superhuman abilities from alternate universe to save Earth from friend turned enemy.
 Chronicle (film): Chronicle is 2012 American found footage science-fiction thriller film directed by Josh Trank written by Max Landis based on story by both follows three Seattle high school seniors, bullied Andrew (Dane DeHaan), cousin Matt (Alex Russell) popular Steve (Michael B. Jordan), form bond after gaining telekinetic powers from unknown object. They first use abilities for mischief personal gain until Andrew turns to darker purposes.
 James Valerio: James Valerio (born 1938) is U.S. artist specializing in photorealist paintings. Valerio educated at School of the Art Institute of Chicago BfA in 1966 MfA in 1968.work included in collection of Butler Institute of American Art other museums.
 The Rapino Brothers: Rapino Brothers are record producers Charlie Mallozzi Marco Sabiu known for work during 1990s with artists like Kylie Minogue, Dannii Minogue, Paola e Chiara, Valerio Scanu, Lydia Canaan Primal Scream.
 Valerio Spada: Valerio Spada (born 1972) is Italian photographer known for book "Gomorrah Girl". In 2013 awarded Guggenheim Fellowship for Creative Arts, Photography. Fellowship awarded in support of work exposing hardships of living in impoverished parts of Italy. Previous Guggenheim Fellows include Robert Frank, Cindy Sherman, John Gossage, Edward Weston Diane Arbus. work exhibited internationally including in US and Europe.

Sleepless in Seattle: Sleepless in Seattle is a 1993 American romantic comedy-drama film directed and co-written by Nora Ephron, based on a story by Jeff Arch. stars Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan, supporting cast featuring Bill Pullman, Ross Malinger, Rob Reiner, Rosie O'Donnell, Gaby Hoffmann, Victor Garber, Rita Wilson. film was a critical and commercial success, grossing over $220 million worldwide.
 Rosie O'Donnell: Roseann O'Donnell (born March 21, 1962) is an American comedian, actress, author, and television personality. She been a magazine editor to a celebrity blogger, lesbian rights activist, television producer, and a collaborative partner in LGBT family vacation company, R Family Vacations.
 Shaheed Woods: Shaheed K. Woods (born Shaheed Kamal Jihad Woods) is an American actor, comedian born and raised in Jersey City, New Jersey. best known for "A Gentleman", "Midnight Delight", "Life! Camera Action..." earning accolades.
 Yannis Pappas: Yannis Pappas is a Greek-American comedian born and raised in Park Slope Brooklyn, New York. Both his parents, Anna and Chris, practiced law. He is youngest of three children. has two older brothers, Peter and Nikos Pappas. His brother Peter is also a lawyer worked for Clinton and Obama administrations. Yannis attended college at American University in Washington, D.C. studied American Studies and History. Pappas previously worked in social work field participated in 9/11 disaster relief for two and a half years and worked with mentally ill and people dealing with homelessness for three years with Lutheran Social Services.
 Tim Bedore: Tim Bedore (born c. 1957) is an American comedian born in Chicago, IL. His parents moved to Stevens Point, Wisconsin when he was a child. attended Pacelli High School (Wisconsin) in Stevens Point and Appleton High School-West, where he graduated.
 Barry Ackerley: Barry Allen Ackerley (April 15, 1934 – March 21, 2011) was an American businessman.He was the former Chairman and CEO of Ackerley Group media company. was owner of Seattle SuperSonics basketball franchise from 1983 to 2001. Ackerley died on March 21, 2011, two days after suffering a stroke.

Rob Sitch: Robert Ian "Rob" Sitch (born 17 March 1962) is an Australian director, producer, screenwriter, actor and comedian.
 Any Questions for Ben?: Any Questions for Ben? is a 2012 Australian comedy film created by Working Dog Productions, directed by Rob Sitch. stars Josh Lawson, Rachael Taylor, Felicity Ward, Daniel Henshall Christian Clark. written by Santo Cilauro, Tom Gleisner and Rob Sitch.
 Clayton Watson: Clayton Watson (born 23 March 1977) is Australian producer, actor, writer, director. grew up in Australian outback on sheep station close to Morgan, small town in South Australia. best known for playing role of Kid next to Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, Carrie-Anne Moss in "The Matrix Reloaded", "The Matrix Revolutions", short film "Kid's Story" in "The Animatrix". reprised role for "The Matrix Online", nominated for Best Newcomer at American Sci-Fi Awards. won an AFI for role in "Always Greener", played lead in two Stephen King films.
 Josh Schuberth: Josh Schuberth (born 23 September 1983) is Australian producer, audio engineer, multi-instrumentalist. list of credits includes work with numerous notable performers, including Ben Folds, Josh Pyke, Alex Lloyd, Jessica Mauboy, Sara Storer, Graeme Connors, Lenka, Melanie Horsnell, Jenny Queen, Suzy Connolly, Tim Freedman, Greg Storer, bands Peregrine and The Sleep-ins. also records as solo performer under name Miracle Pill.
 Bad Dreems: Bad Dreems (stylised as Bad//Dreems) are an "outsider rock" band from Adelaide, South Australia.band consists of Ben Marwe (Vocals/Guitar), Alex Cameron (Guitar), James Bartold (Bass), and Miles Wilson (Drums). band released debut EP titled "Badlands" in August 2013. released debut album "Dogs at Bay" on 21 August 2015 with legendary Australian producer Mark Opitz (INXS, Cold Chisel, the Angels).
 Inside Film Awards: Inside Film Awards (now known as the IF Awards) is an annual awards ceremony and broadcast platform for Australian film industry, developed by creators of Inside Film Magazine, Stephen Jenner and David Barda, originally produced for television by Australian Producer Andrew Dillon. awards are determined by national audience poll, differentiates it from Australian AACTA Awards, judged by industry professionals.
 Trish Lake: Trish Lake is an Australian producer of feature films and documentaries and former ABC TV journalist. Among her works are "Gettin' Square "(2003)", The Burning Season "(2008) and "Frackman" (2015). She is CEO of Freshwater Pictures, based in Brisbane, Queensland, she founded in 2001. Lake was National President of Screen Producer’s Association of Australia – SPAA from 2005 - 2008 a former recipient of SPAA Feature Film Producer of the Year award. Lake is Adjunct Fellow at Griffith University, Brisbane leads mentoring program for emerging producers at Griffith Film School. Lake been advisor to Breath of Fresh Air Film Festival (BOFA) in Tasmania since inception, event's artistic director since 2012. collaborated professionally with nephew Daniel (Dan) Lake on many productions. Dan Lake left Freshwater Pictures in November 2014 to take on position as a director of production investment at Screen Queensland.

The Shins: Shins are an American indie rock band from Albuquerque, New Mexico, formed in 1996. band's current lineup consists of James Mercer (vocals, guitar, songwriter), Jon Sortland (drums), Mark Watrous (guitar), Casey Foubert (guitar), Yuuki Matthews (bass), Patti King (keyboards). band based in Portland, Oregon.
 Broken Bells: Broken Bells is American indie rock band composed of artist-producer Brian Burton (better known as Danger Mouse) and James Mercer, lead vocalist and guitarist for indie rock band The Shins. Broken Bells compose and create as duo, joined by Dan Elkan and Jon Sortland when performing live. previous live band included Conor Oberst and Mystic Valley Band sidemen Nate Walcott and Nik Freitas, and Jonathan Hischke and Dan Elkan, both ex-members of Hella. Following 2010 self-titled debut album, duo released EP, "Meyrin Fields", in 2011 and second studio album, "After the Disco", on February 4, 2014.
 Jon Sortland: Jon Sortland (born September 12, 1973) is American musician, currently playing drums for indie rock band The Shins. Sortland also drums, plays bass and keyboards and provides backing vocals in band Broken Bells. Sortland is also drummer and singer in band E V Kain. Sortland endorsed by Paiste and C&C Drums.
 Jesse Sandoval: Jesse Sandoval is former drummer of American indie rock group The Shins. Sandoval formed Flake with singer-songwriter James Mercer, guitarist Neal Langford bassist Marty Crandall in Albuquerque, New Mexico in 1992. Sandoval and Mercer then on to form The Shins as a side project, intending to play as a duo, but eventually joined again by Marty Crandall on keyboard and Dave Hernandez on bass. Sandoval, along with other band members, now resides in Portland, Oregon.
Port of Morrow (album): Port of Morrow is fourth studio album by American rock band The Shins. album released March 19, 2012, on Aural Apothecary and Columbia Records co-produced by Greg Kurstin and frontman James Mercer. The Shins' first studio album in five years, following release of 2007's "Wincing the Night Away", followed major lineup changes in the group: founding members Dave Hernandez (bass, guitar), Marty Crandall (keyboards) and Jesse Sandoval (drums) departed in 2009. Mercer deemed it an "aesthetic decision" to part ways with bandmates, and in the interim, founded side project Broken Bells with Danger Mouse.
 Wizard of Ahhhs: Wizard of Ahhhs is an EP by American indie rock group Black Kids, released by the band in August 2007 via free download on official MySpace page. In November band launched official website, EP was available for download until March 2008. EP recorded at The Glow Studio in the spring of 2007 by fellow Jacksonville musician Jesse Mangum (Jesse and The Glow Studio since relocated to Athens, GA.) Some other demo tracks recorded during sessions leaked on internet: "Listen to Your Body Tonight", "Designs on AKA You", "I Wanna Be Your Limousine", and "Love Me Already".

Braathens: Braathens ASA, until 1997 Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A/S and trading as Braathens SAFE, was a Norwegian airline operated from 1946 until merged with Scandinavian Airlines Norway (SAS) in 2004 to become SAS Braathens. For most of history, Braathens was the largest domestic airline in Norway, but did not operate international network for many years. main hubs were Oslo Airport, Fornebu later Oslo Airport, Gardermoen, and briefly Stockholm-Arlanda Airport. airline operated 118 aircraft of 15 models, majority of variations of Boeing 737. Braathens served 53 airports and 50 cities with scheduled services through history.
 Scandinavian Airlines: Scandinavian Airlines, usually shortened to SAS (originally abbreviation of former name Scandinavian Airlines System or legally Scandinavian Airlines System Denmark–Norway–Sweden) is flag carrier of Sweden, Norway and Denmark.
 SAS Braathens: SAS Braathens was name of Norway's largest airline, created by merger between Scandinavian Airlines' Norwegian division and Braathens in 2004. On June 1, 2007, airline integrated into mainline SAS, changed name to SAS Scandinavian Airlines Norge. airline operated from hub at Oslo Airport, Gardermoen, was also largest national branch of Scandinavian Airlines. SAS Braathens had head office in Diamanten on grounds of Fornebu Airport in Fornebu, Bærum, Norway.
 History of Braathens (1994–2004): Braathens SAFE's domestic market was deregulated on 1 April 1994. Since then, any airline within European Economic Area is free to operate any domestic or international route. Braathens rejected proposal from main competitor Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) for merger; instead helicopter division was sold and company listed on Oslo Stock Exchange. New routes opened from Oslo Airport, Fornebu to Bodø, Harstad/Narvik and Tromsø, but routes from Bergen to these cities terminated. International routes to Rome, Nice and Jersey were introduced.In 1996, Braathens SAFE bought Sweden's second-largest airline, Transwede, started flying on Oslo–Stockholm route. following year, Transwede, with five domestic routes, merged into Braathens SAFE. same year, KLM bought 30% of Braathens SAFE airlines started partnership.
 Braathens Helikopter: Braathens Helikopter A/S was a Norwegian helicopter airline based at Stavanger Airport, Sola, and Bergen Airport, Flesland. used a fleet of seven Aérospatiale Super Pumas to serve offshore oil platforms in North Sea. customers were Phillips Petroleum, Norsk Hydro, Statoil, Amoco British Petroleum, serving oil fields Ekofisk, Oseberg, Gullfaks, Veslefrikk, Valhall, Ula and Gyda. Braathens Helikopter operated from 1989 to 1993, after sold to and merged with main competitor, Helikopter Service. Braathens Helikopter was owned by Ludvig G. Braathens Rederi was a sister company of airline Braathens SAFE.

Mach number: In fluid dynamics Mach number (M or Ma) ( ; ] ) is dimensionless quantity representing ratio of flow velocity past boundary to local speed of sound.
 Saab JAS 39 Gripen: Saab JAS 39 Gripen (English: "griffin" ) is light single-engine multirole fighter aircraft manufactured by Swedish aerospace company Saab designed to replace Saab 35 Draken and 37 Viggen in Swedish Air Force ("Flygvapnet"). Gripen has delta wing canard configuration relaxed stability design fly-by-wire flight controls powered by Volvo RM12 top speed of Mach 2. aircraft modified for NATO interoperability standards undertake in-flight refuelling.
 Pitot tube: Pitot ( ) tube also known as Pitot probe, is pressure measurement instrument measure fluid flow velocity. pitot tube invented by French engineer Henri Pitot early 18th century modified to modern form mid-19th century by French scientist Henry Darcy. used to determine airspeed of aircraft, water speed of boat measure liquid, air gas flow velocities in certain industrial applications. pitot tube used measure local flow velocity at given point in flow stream not average flow velocity in pipe or conduit.
 A-Darter: V3E A-Darter (Agile Darter) is modern short-range infrared homing ("heat seeking") air-to-air missile countermeasures resistance 180-degree look angle 120-degrees per second track rate developed by South Africa's Denel Dynamics (formerly Kentron) Brazil's Mectron, Avibras and Opto Eletrônica. will equip South African Air Force's Saab JAS 39 Gripen C/D BAe Hawk 120; Brazilian Air Force's A-1M AMX, Northrop F-5BR Gripen E/F. expected to in production before end of 2015.
Saab 38: Saab 38 (also known as B3LA or A 38/Sk 38) was a single-engine jet trainer and attack aircraft planned by Saab during 1970s. project was collaboration between Saab and Italian aircraft manufacturer Aermacchi. to replace older Saab 105 jet trainer in Swedish Air Force, but aircraft never past drawing board canceled in 1979 in favour of advanced Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighter.
 Bombkapsel 90: Bombkapsel 90 (BK90) is Swedish Air Force's nomenclature for gliding stand-off submunitions dispenser, or cluster bomb, with 72 submunitions. manufactured by DaimlerChrysler Aerospace in Germany of DWS 24 - "Dispenser Weapon System 24 barrels". BK90 also known as DWS 39 "Mjölner" intended for use with Saab JAS 39 Gripen. future could be also integrated on Eurofighter Typhoon. design similar to American AGM-154 Joint Standoff Weapon.

SWX Right Now: (Sports and Weather Right Now) is digital subchannel broadcasting high school college sports automated weather information to viewers Eastern Washington state. channel operated by Cowles Company airs over Cowles' three NBC affiliated channels in Eastern Washington including Spokane's KHQ, KNDO Yakima Richland's KNDU, Billings' KULR in Montana on most cable systems markets serve.
 KKBR: KKBR (97.1 FM) - operating as 97.1 Kiss FM - commercial radio station in Billings, Montana. Licensed to Billings, Montana station serves Billings area. owned by Townsquare Media Billings License, LLC. station obtained construction permit from FCC for power increase to 100,000 watts.
 KEWF: KEWF commercial radio station in Billings, Montana broadcasting on 98.5 FM. KEWF airs country music format “98.5 The Wolf”. station formerly KGHL- FM before KGHL- AM 790 sold to Northern Broadcasting System. Licensed to Billings, Montana station serves Billings area owned by Radio Billings, LLC.
 KULR-TV: KULR-TV, virtual channel 8, is NBC affiliate broadcasting on channel 11 in Billings, Montana. KULR owned by Cowles Company. KULR maintains studios on Overland Avenue in Homestead Business Park section of Billings transmitter on Coburn Hill southeast of downtown Billings.
 KBXI: KBXI (92.5 FM, "MoJo 92.5") commercial radio station licensed in Park City, Montana to Billings, Montana, area KBXI airs adult hits music format Licensed City station serves Billings area. station owned by local radio personality Kurt Anthony, through licensee Anthony Media Inc. Anthony also operates Twang 107.5 and Crossroads 105.1.
KCTR-FM: (102.9 FM, "Cat Country 103") commercial radio station Billings, Montana KCTR airs country music format Licensed to Billings, Montana station serves Billings area owned by Townsquare Media Billings License, LLC.
 KRSQ: KRSQ (101.9 MHz) commercial radio station Laurel, Montana serving Billings, Montana area airs CHR music format “Hot 101.9”. Licensed to Laurel, Montana serves Billings area owned by Radio Billings, LLC.
 KXMD-TV: KXMD-TV, channel 11, CBS affiliate for Williston, North Dakota. station operates semi-satellite of KXMC-TV in Minot, North Dakota outlet broadcasts high definition digital signal on UHF channel 14 (or virtual channel 11.1 via PSIP) from transmitter west of Williston near North Dakota/Montana border. KXMD identifies as station in its own right simulcasts all programming from KXMC KXMD airs separate commercials station identifications. station maintains news bureau advertising sales office at intersection 13th Avenue West and 18th Street West (near U.S. Highway 2/85) in Williston. KXMD's viewing area includes most Montana portion market. Montana within Mountain Time Zone, primetime programming KXMD begins at 6 pm rather than 7 pm for other stations Central Time Zone. station seen on Midcontinent cable channel 6 in Williston, cable channel 11 most other areas. high definition feed provided on Midcontinent digital channel 606.

Mookie Blaylock: Daron Oshay "Mookie" Blaylock (born March 20, 1967) is an American retired professional basketball player. He spent 13 years in the National Basketball Association (NBA) with three different teams, namely the New Jersey Nets, Atlanta Hawks, and Golden State Warriors.
 1995–96 Atlanta Hawks season: The 1995–96 NBA season was the Hawks' 47th season in the National Basketball Association, and 28th season in Atlanta. During the offseason, Hawks re-acquired Spud Webb from the Sacramento Kings. Hawks played above .500 during the first month of season, but then struggled losing 10 of their 14 games in December before posting a ten-game winning streak in January. At midseason, Webb was traded along with Andrew Lang to Minnesota Timberwolves for Christian Laettner and Sean Rooks. Hawks finished fourth in the Central Division with a 46–36 record. Head coach Lenny Wilkens reached a significant milestone, becoming the first NBA coach to reach 1,000 victories. Steve Smith led the Hawks in scoring averaging 18.1 points per game, and Mookie Blaylock finished third in the league with 231 three-point field goals, which was a franchise record for the team.
 George T. Johnson: George Thomas Johnson (born December 18, 1948) is an American retired professional basketball player. A 6'11" forward/center born in Tylertown, Mississippi and from Dillard University, he played in 13 NBA seasons (1972–1983; 1984–1986) as a member of Golden State Warriors, Buffalo Braves, New Jersey Nets, San Antonio Spurs, the Atlanta Hawks, and the Seattle SuperSonics.
 Chris Engler: Chris Engler (born March 1, 1959) is an American former National Basketball Association (NBA) player. Engler was drafted from the University of Wyoming by the Golden State Warriors in the third round of the 1982 NBA draft. Engler began his collegiate career with Minnesota Golden Gophers before transferring to Wyoming.Engler played two seasons with Warriors, then subsequently had short stints with the Milwaukee Bucks, Chicago Bulls, New Jersey Nets, and Portland Trail Blazers before staying with Nets for final two seasons of his NBA career. Engler finished with career averages of 1.8 points per game and 2.0 rebounds per game.
 Splash Brothers: The Splash Brothers are a duo of American basketball players consisting of Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson. The two guards play professionally for Golden State Warriors in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Excellent long-range shooters, they have combined to set various NBA records for three-point field goals by a pair of teammates, and each has won the Three-Point Contest. The two NBA All-Stars won NBA championship with the Warriors in 2015 and 2017.
 Garry St. Jean: Garry St. Jean (born February 10, 1950 in Chicopee, Massachusetts) is an American former professional basketball coach and executive. St. Jean was head coach of the Sacramento Kings from 1992 through 1997. He later became the general manager of Golden State Warriors, and in 1999–2000 doubled as a head coach after P.J. Carlesimo was fired. St. Jean was a pro scout for New Jersey Nets in the 2010–11 season. He has been an in-studio analyst for Golden State Warriors coverage on Comcast SportsNet Bay Area since the start of 2011-2012 season.

Chrysler: FCA US LLC (also called Fiat Chrysler or Chrysler) ( ) is the American subsidiary of Fiat Chrysler Automobiles N.V., an Italian controlled automobile manufacturer registered in the Netherlands with headquarters in London, U.K., for tax purposes. FCA US is one of the "Big Three" American automobile manufacturers. FCA US has headquarters in Auburn Hills, Michigan and sells vehicles worldwide under its flagship Chrysler brand, as the Dodge, Jeep, and Ram Trucks. Other major divisions include Mopar, automotive parts and accessories division, and SRT, performance automobile division.
 Ramos Arizpe: Ramos Arizpe (] ) is a city and seat of surrounding municipality of the same name in the Mexican state of Coahuila. Ramos Arizpe is located 11 km from the state capital of Saltillo. It is part of Saltillo metropolitan area. city reported a population of 48,228 in the 2005 census; municipality had a population of 56,708. Its area is 5,306.6 km2 (2,048.9 sq mi).
 Saltillo Engine Plant: Saltillo Engine is a Chrysler engine plant in Ramos Arizpe, Coahuila, Mexico. factory opened in 1981. It was built as a scale model of the plant at Trenton, Michigan, United States, but with more work flexibility, having only 20 job classifications rather than 70 at Trenton.
 GM High Value engine: The High Value engine family from General Motors is a group of Cam in Block or "Overhead valve" V6 engines. They use the same 60° vee bank as 60° V6 family based on, but new 99 mm bore required offsetting bores by 1.5 mm away from engine centerline. These engines (aside from LX9) are first cam in block engines to implement Variable Valve Timing, and won the 2006 Breakthrough Award from "Popular Mechanics" for this innovation. For the 2007 model year, the 3900 engine features optional displacement on demand or "Active Fuel Management" which deactivates a bank of cylinders under light load to increase highway fuel economy.rumored GM would produce a 3-valve design, but that never came to be. These engines were produced primarily at the GM factory in Tonawanda, New York and at Ramos Arizpe engine plant in Mexico. assembly line for this engine was manufactured by Hirata Corporation at their powertrain facility in Kumamoto, Japan.

Dean Winchester: Dean Winchester is a fictional character and one of the two protagonists of the American drama television series "Supernatural". He is portrayed by Jensen Ackles. Other versions of character been portrayed by Hunter Brochu (toddler), Ridge Canipe (child), Nicolai Lawton-Giustra (pre-teen), Brock Kelly and Dylan Everett (teen), and Chad Everett (elderly).
 Wingin' It: Wingin' It (originally titled Angel on Campus prior to debut) is a Canadian teen sitcom aired on Family. series produced by Temple Street Productions in association with Family. It stars Demetrius Joyette and Dylan Everett. This show included guest-stars from other Family Channel shows such as "The Latest Buzz". announced series was renewed for a third season on June 13, 2011. Family announced series is not planned for a fourth season.
 Frenemies (film): Frenemies is a 2012 teen comedy-drama television film and anthology based on the novel of the same name by Alexa Young premiered on Disney Channel. It features an ensemble cast starring Bella Thorne, Zendaya, Stefanie Scott, Nick Robinson, Mary Mouser and features Connor Price, Jascha Washington and Dylan Everett. film follows three pairs of teenage friends go from friends to enemies and back again. film was directed by Daisy Mayer and written by Dava Savel, Wendy Weiner, and Jim Krieg. The Disney Channel Original Movie premiered on January 13, 2012 in the United States and Canada.
 Dylan Everett: Dylan Everett (born January 24, 1995) is a Canadian actor. best known for his roles in "How To Be Indie" (2009–2011), "Wingin' It" (2010–2013), "" (2012–2013), and "Open Heart" (2015).
 Open Heart (TV series): Open Heart is a 2015 American-Canadian mystery-drama television series produced by Epitome Pictures unit of DHX Media in association with marblemedia. It first aired on January 20, 2015, on TeenNick in the United States and previously on YTV; now currently on ABC Spark in Canada.
The Roy Files: The Roy Files is an Irish-based British children's television show, filmed in Dublin, Ireland, broadcast by CBBC in the United Kingdom and ABC Me in Australia. began airing 7 December 2015. show centres on the title character Roy O'Brien, the 11-year-old animated son of a live-action family. series is a spin-off from "ROY", an Irish-British television show ran from 1 July 2009 to 7 April 2015. It stars Jason Cullen (replacing Scott Graham as Roy), Simon Delaney, Cathy Belton and Martha Byrne.

Chaerophyllum elegans: Chaerophyllum elegans is a flowering plant species in genus "Chaerophyllum" found in Alps from Switzerland, France Italy.
 Chaerophyllum: Chaerophyllum is a genus of flowering plant in Apiaceae, with 35 species native to Europe, Asia, North America, northern Africa. includes cultivated root vegetable "Chaerophyllum bulbosum" (turnip rooted chervil).
 Cryptanthus: Cryptanthus is a genus in botanical family Bromeliaceae, subfamily Bromelioideae. genus name is from Greek “cryptos” (hidden) and “anthos” (flower). genus has two recognized subgenera: type subgenus and "Hoplocryptanthus" . All species genus are endemic to Brazil. common name for "Cryptanthus" is "Earth Star".
 Quakers in Europe: Quaker movement began in England in Seventeenth Century. Small Quaker groups planted in various places across Europe during early period (For instance, see Stephen Crisp article). Quakers in Europe outside Britain and Ireland not now very numerous new groups started in former Soviet Union and satellite countries. largest national grouping of Quakers in Europe is in Britain.
 Leontodon taraxacoides: Leontodon taraxacoides is species of hawkbit known by common name lesser hawkbit, rough hawkbit, or hairy hawkbit. native to Europe and North Africa can be found in many other places across globe as introduced species and often noxious weed. dandelion-like herb growing patches of many erect, leafless stems from basal rosette of leaves. leaves are 2 to 15 centimeters long, 0.5 to 2.5 centimeters wide, entire or lobed, green in color. Atop stems are solitary flower heads ligulate, containing layered rings of ray florets with no disc florets. florets are yellow with toothed tips. fruit is a cylindrical achene with pappus of scales.Fruits near center of flower head are rough, those growing along edges of head are smooth.
 Angiopteris evecta: Angiopteris evecta, commonly known as the giant fern, is rare plant occurring in eastern and northern Australia and Malay Peninsula. Also found growing in nearby islands Borneo, Sumatra, New Guinea various places in Polynesia, Melanesia and Madagascar. Listed as endangered in New South Wales, recorded growing in sub tropical rainforest, in valley of Tweed River. invasive species in Hawaii and Jamaica.
 Ground stable barn: Ground stable barns are modern type of barn design found in many places across United States. Mostly constructed after 1910 when government health regulations associated with dairy industry altered forcing changes in barn design.
 Mary Hanford Ford: Mary Hanford Ford (November 1, 1856 – February 2, 1937) was an American lecturer, author, art and literature critic leader in women's suffrage movement. reached early notoriety in Kansas at age of 28 soon left for Chicago World's Fair. taken up by society ladies of Chicago area who, impressed with her talks on art and literature at Fair, helped launch her on new career, initially in Chicago and then across some States. she was already published in articles and noticed in suffrage meetings. In addition to work as art critic and speaker wrote number of books, most prominently trilogy "Message of the Mystics". Circa 1900-1902 Ford found Bahá'í Faith through Sarah Farmer, Green Acre, and Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, helped form first community of Bahá'ís in Boston where Louis Bourgeois, future architect of first Bahá'í House of Worship in West, joined religion. In 1907 Ford went on Bahá'í pilgrimage, in 1910 she started writing Bahá'í books such as "The Oriental Rose", traveled with `Abdu'l-Bahá during of his journeys in various places in Europe and then America.Ford blamed for a fiasco among UK suffragists but was their own violence got them in trouble. Ford spent years of World War I in California following first Bahá'í International Congress at Panama–Pacific International Exposition, then moved back to New York she spent almost next 20 years. Often traveled to Europe for some months of year during period introduced religion to Ugo Giachery, later a prominent Bahá'í. in this period she was censored off radio broadcast, helped develop religion's community in meetings she supported and literary efforts, before reducing her travels and speaking engagements in early 1930s. She died with her daughter by her bedside in 1937.

Tropicana Casino & Resort Atlantic City: The Tropicana Casino & Resort Atlantic City is a luxury hotel, casino, and spa resort located on Brighton Avenue and the Boardwalk in Atlantic City, New Jersey. It is owned by Tropicana Entertainment and is one of the largest hotels in New Jersey with over 2,000 rooms. Tropicana has over 3,000 slot machines and 135 table games features The Quarter, a shopping mall located in the complex.
 Caesars Atlantic City: Caesars Atlantic City is a luxury hotel, casino, and spa resort in Atlantic City, New Jersey. Like Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, it has an ancient Roman and ancient Greek theme. Atlantic City's second casino, opened in 1979 as the Caesars Boardwalk Regency. The 124720 sqft . casino has over 3,400 slot machines, is one of the largest in Atlantic City. resort has experienced much expansion and renovation in the past decade, including a new hotel tower, new parking garage, and a new shopping center, Playground Pier. Known to many visit Atlantic City as the present day "Hub" of the boardwalk.
 Johnny Mathis: Wonderful, Wonderful!: Johnny Mathis: Wonderful, Wonderful! is a television concert by American pop singer Johnny Mathis recorded on October 27, 2006, at the Tropicana Hotel in Atlantic City and aired that December on most PBS stations. In to singing some of his biggest hits, he covers tracks from his live albums ("In the Morning" from "" and "To the Ends of the Earth" from "Unforgettable – A Musical Tribute to Nat King Cole"), songs from Brazil ("Manhã de Carnaval" from "Olé" and "Brazil (Aquarela do Brasil)" from "The Ultimate Hits Collection"), and two exclusives ("Let Go (Canto de ossanho)" and "Pure Imagination") that have never appeared on a Mathis album. Interview clips with Mathis were inserted at intervals throughout the concert along with live performance excerpts from programs such as "The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson" and "The Andy Williams Show".
MGM Grand Atlantic City: MGM Grand Atlantic City was a planned resort casino by MGM Mirage in Atlantic City, New Jersey. It to be located on 72 acre of land between Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa (which MGM Mirage owns 50%) and Harrah's Atlantic City.
 Borgata: Borgata Hotel Casino & Spa is a hotel, casino, and spa in Atlantic City, New Jersey, United States. It owned and operated by MGM Resorts International. casino hotel features 2,002 rooms and is the largest hotel in New Jersey. Borgata opened in July 2003 and is the top-grossing casino in Atlantic City.

In His Eyes: "In His Eyes" is a song performed in musical "Jekyll and Hyde", composed by Frank Wildhorn with lyrics by Frank Wildhorn, Leslie Bricusse Steve Cuden. "Jekyll and Hyde" premiered on Broadway in 1997 since seen many subsequent international regional, productions. In 2013, show revived on Broadway song appeared in Original Broadway production performed by Linda Eder and Christiane Noll.
 Bill Grainer: Bill Grainer is a Grammy certified American songwriter and producer. written for artists Jai McDowall, Linda Eder, Jennifer Hudson, with co-wrote song "Stand Up" for her Grammy Award-winning self-titled debut album.
 Rebecca Spencer (singer): Rebecca Spencer is an American singer and actress known for roles in musicals on concert and cabaret stages. career performed principal roles in over 50 opera, national tour, regional Off-Broadway productions. She created role of Lisa Carew in world premiere of Frank Wildhorn's Jekyll and Hyde at the Alley Theatre, opposite Linda Eder and Chuck Wagner, premiered role of Madame Giry in $35 million production of Phantom - The Las Vegas Spectacular, under direction of Harold Prince.
 Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre is performing arts venue located in Cumberland/Galleria edge city, northwest of Atlanta, Georgia $145 million facility celebrated grand opening September 15, 2007, with concert by Michael Feinstein and Linda Eder.
 Anne Cochran: Anne Cochran is a singer-songwriter from Cleveland, Ohio.best known as lead touring vocalist for pianist songwriter Jim Brickman, with shared top 5 Adult Contemporary radio format hit single "After All These Years" in 1998. released solo albums, single "Someone Is Missing at Christmas" from her album "This is the Season" peaked at number 11 on US Adult contemporary chart in 2005. shared duets with musicians artists Donny Osmond, Michael Feinstein, Collin Raye, Dave Koz, Richie McDonald, Orlagh Fallon, Tracy Silverman, Jeff Timmons, Kristy Starling, Mario Frangoulis, Wayne Brady, Michael Bolton, Linda Eder Mark Masri.
 Belleayre Music Festival: Belleayre Music Festival is an annual festival in Catskill Mountains of Upstate New York Founded in Highmount, NY, Phyllis and Mel Litoff raised prominence of festival after becoming co-artistic directors in 1993. Since then festival hosted artists as James Blunt, Rosanne Cash, Branford Marsalis, Frankie Valli, Obie Benson, Lyle Lovett, The Neville Brothers, Linda Eder, Ray Charles, Wynton Marsalis.

Azusa Pacific University: Azusa Pacific University (APU) is a private, evangelical Christian university located near Los Angeles in suburban Azusa, California, United States. university was founded in 1899, with classes opening on March 3, 1900, in Whittier, California, began offering degrees in 1939. university's seminary, the Graduate School of Theology, holds to Wesleyan-Arminian doctrinal theology. APU offers more than 100 associate, bachelor's, master's, and doctoral programs on campus, online, and at seven regional locations across Southern California.
 Diana Pavlac Glyer: Diana Pavlac Glyer (born 21 January 1956 in Aberdeen, Maryland) is a United States author, speaker, and teacher whose work centers on C. S. Lewis, J. R. R. Tolkien, and the Inklings.
 The Company They Keep: The Company They Keep: C. S. Lewis and J. R. R. Tolkien as Writers in Community (2007) is a non-fiction book written by Diana Pavlac Glyer, an Inklings scholar and English professor at Azusa Pacific University. "The Company They Keep" challenges commonly belief that the Inklings did not influence each other through a detailed engaging examination of published and unpublished works, papers, and letters written by J.R.R. Tolkien, C.S. Lewis, Charles Williams, Owen Barfield, Warren Lewis and lesser-known writers who comprised the Inklings.
 John Culp: John Culp is a professor works at the Azusa Pacific University in the Department of Philosophy. specializes in the philosophy of religion, history of philosophy and Wesleyan theology. written for the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
 Peter L. Berger: Peter Ludwig Berger (March 17, 1929 – June 27, 2017), an Austrian-born American sociologist and Protestant theologian, became known for his work in the sociology of knowledge, sociology of religion, study of modernization, and theoretical contributions to sociological theory.He arguably best known for his book, co-authored with Thomas Luckmann, "The Social Construction of Reality: A Treatise in the Sociology of Knowledge" (New York, 1966), considered one of most influential texts in the sociology of knowledge, played central role in development of social constructionism. In 1998 International Sociological Association named this book as the fifth most-influential book written in the field of sociology during the 20th century. In addition to this book, the other books Berger written include: "" (1963); "" (1969); and "The Sacred Canopy: Elements of a Social Theory of Religion" (1967). Berger spent most of his career teaching at The New School for Social Research, at Rutgers University, and at Boston University. Before retiring, Berger had been at Boston University since 1981 and was the director of the Institute for the Study of Economic Culture.
 Smadar Lavie: Smadar Lavie (Hebrew: סמדר לביא ) is a Mizrahi U.S.-Israeli anthropologist, author, and activist. She specializes in the anthropology of Egypt, Israel and Palestine, emphasizing issues of race, gender and religion. Lavie is a Scholar in Residence at the Beatrice Bain Research Group of the University of California, Berkeley’s Department of Gender and Women’s Studies (2012-2016), and a visiting professor at , University College Cork (2011–16). Lavie received her doctorate in Anthropology from the University of California at Berkeley (1989) and spent nine years as Assistant and Associate Professor of Anthropology at the University of California, Davis. She authored "The Poetics of Military Occupation" (UC Press, 1990), receiving 1990 Honorable Mention of the Victor Turner Award for Ethnographic Writing, and "Wrapped in the Flag of Israel: Mizrahi Single Mothers and Bureaucratic Torture" (Berghahn Books 2014), receiving 2015 Honorable Mention of the Association of Middle East Women’s Studies Book Award Competition."Wrapped in the Flag of Israel" was one of four finalists in the 2015 Clifford Geertz Book Award Competition of Society for the Anthropology of Religion. She co-edited "Creativity/Anthropology" (Cornell UP, 1993) and "Displacement, Diaspora, and Geographies of Identity" (Duke UP, 1996). Lavie won the American Studies Association’s 2009 Gloria Anzaldúa Prize for her article, “Staying Put: Crossing Palestine-Israel Border with Gloria Anzaldúa,” published in "Anthropology" and "Humanism" (2011). In 2013, Smadar Lavie won the “Heart at East” Honor Plaque for lifetime service to Mizraḥi communities in Israel-Palestine.

For One Night Only (Irish TV series): Irish light entertainment show hosted by Gay Byrne features music chat with special guest musician studio-based show aired Friday nights as summer "filler" in 2011. returned for second series in 2012.
 Gay Byrne: Gabriel Mary "Gay" Byrne (born 5 August 1934 known as Uncle Gay, Gaybo or Uncle Gaybo) is Irish presenter of radio and television notable role first host of "The Late Late Show" over 37-year period 1962 until 1999. world's second longest-running chat show working in Britain with Granada Television first person to introduce Beatles on screen
 One Night Only (TV series): British entertainment show celebrating best of British Music. Myleene Klass hosted first episode December 2008 with singer Tom Jones. Ben Shephard hosted in 2009 and 2010, Rod Stewart and Phil Collins stage. November 2010, Fearne Cotton hosted one-off special with Bon Jovi 2011 presented by Christine Bleakley featuring music from Duran Duran. Another episode aired November 2014, with Rob Brydon hosting "Neil Diamond: One Night Only". Joanna Lumley presented seventh episode with Bette Midler in December 2014.
 Elton John One Night Only – The Greatest Hits: Only live album released by Elton John in 2000. recorded on 20 and 21 October 2000 at Madison Square Garden. extended version released as DVD One Night Only: The Greatest Hits Live at Madison Square Garden title "one night only" because recording equipment failed to tape audio from first night leaving only second night recorded as album. US certified gold in July 2001 by RIAA.
You and Me (One Night Only song): "You and Me" is song by One Night Only from 2008 album "Started a Fire", released debut single October 29, 2007. released on 7" vinyl and CD reaching #46 following weeks UK singles chart. B-side for CD is "What's Your Melody". vinyls have "Nintendo" or "Go Go Go". video for "You and Me" posted on MySpace well received MySpace asked band to make short film, "One Night Only Welcomes You to Helmsley". MySpace featured artist on homepage. October and November 2007, One Night Only supported The Pigeon Detectives on tour. December 2007, embarked on own headline tour.
 WWE Extreme Rules: (simply known as Extreme Rules) is professional wrestling event produced annually by WWE, Connecticut-based promotion broadcast live through pay-per-view (PPV) and WWE Network. name event stems from matches contested under hardcore wrestling regulations; defunct Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW) promotion used term to describe regulations for matches event name established in 2009 theme began with predecessor, One Night Stand promoted in 2005 and 2006 as ECW reunion show In 2007, WWE promoted show as regular PPV events but kept ECW concept of Extreme Rules matches. 2009, WWE renamed One Night Stand event to WWE Extreme Rules. 2009 Extreme Rules event direct continuation of One Night Stand chronology 2010 event promoted as only second event under new chronology no longer direct continuation of One Night Stand events Starting 2010, Extreme Rules moved from June to late April/early May to replace Backlash as post-WrestleMania pay-per-view event.For 2013, event scheduled to take place in mid-May replace Over the Limit, moved to October before discontinued later year replaced by Battleground event will return to early June slot of WWE's pay-per-view calendar Raw-exclusive pay-per-view event.

Blood and Soil: Blood soil (German: "Blut und Boden" ) is a slogan expressing nineteenth-century German idealization of racially defined national body ("blood") united with settlement area ("soil"). rural and farm life forms idealized as counterweight to urban ones, combined with racist and anti-Semitic ideas of sedentary Germanic-Nordic peasantry opposed to (specifically Jewish) nomadism. contemporary German concept Lebensraum, belief German people needed to reclaim historically German areas of Eastern Europe expand, is tied to it.
 Nazi Germany: Nazi Germany is common English name for period in German history from 1933 to 1945, when Germany governed by dictatorship under control of Adolf Hitler and Nazi Party (NSDAP). Under Hitler's rule, Germany transformed into totalitarian state in Nazi Party controlled nearly all aspects of life. official name state was "Deutsches Reich" from 1933 to 1943 and "Großdeutsches Reich" ("Greater German Reich") from 1943 to 1945. period also known under names Third Reich (German: "Drittes Reich" ) and National Socialist Period (German: "Zeit des Nationalsozialismus" abbreviated as "NS-Zeit"). Nazi regime end after Allied Powers defeated Germany in May 1945, ending World War II in Europe.
 Lebensraum: German concept of Lebensraum ( English: "living space" ) refers to policies and practices of settler colonialism proliferated in Germany from 1890s to 1940s. First popularized around 1901, "Lebensraum" became a geopolitical goal of Imperial Germany in World War I (1914–1918) as core element of "Septemberprogramm" of territorial expansion. <ref name="E/N301"> </ref> most extreme form of ideology supported by Nazi Party (NSDAP) and Nazi Germany until end of World War II.
Martin Heidegger and Nazism: Philosopher Martin Heidegger joined Nazi Party (NSDAP) on May 1, 1933, ten days after elected Rector of University of Freiburg. A year later, in April 1934, resigned Rectorship stopped taking part in Nazi Party meetings, but remained member of Nazi Party until its dismantling at end of World War II. denazification hearings after World War II led to Heidegger's dismissal from Freiburg, banning him from teaching. In 1949, after years of investigation French military classified Heidegger as a "Mitläufer" or "Nazi follower". teaching ban lifted in 1951 Heidegger granted "emeritus" status in 1953, but never allowed to resume philosophy chair.
 Otto Telschow: Otto Telschow (27 February 1876, Wittenberge, Brandenburg – 31 May 1945), German Nazi Party official, born in Wittenberge became police official in Hamburg. Telschow joined German Social Party in 1905. In 1925 joined Nazi Party, founder of regional Nazi newspaper, "Niedersachsen-Stürmer". In October 1928 Telschow appointed Gauleiter (regional party leader) of Nazi party's regional subsection Gau Eastern Hanover, post retained until end of World War II. Telschow gained more influence after 1935, when Nazi-party "Gaue" usurped functions of streamlined German states. In 1930 elected to Reichstag for Ost-Hannover electoral district, remained member until 1945. taken prisoner by British Army at Lüneburg committed suicide in prison by slashing his wrists.

The Visit (2015 American film): The Visit is a 2015 American found footage horror film written directed by M. Night Shyamalan starring Olivia DeJonge, Ed Oxenbould, Deanna Dunagan, Peter McRobbie, Kathryn Hahn.
 Scare Campaign: Scare Campaign is a 2016 Australian horror film written directed by Colin and Cameron Cairnes starring Meegan Warner, Ian Meadows, Olivia DeJonge Josh Quong Tart.
 Olivia DeJonge: Olivia DeJonge (born 30 April 1998) is an Australian actress known for playing Tara Swift / Shaneen Quigg in series "Hiding" and Becca in film "The Visit".
 Signs (film): Signs is a 2002 American science fiction horror film written directed by M. Night Shyamalan executive produced by Shyamalan, Frank Marshall, Kathleen Kennedy Sam Mercer. joint collective effort film production made by Blinding Edge Pictures and The Kennedy/Marshall Company. commercially distributed by Touchstone Pictures theatrically, by Touchstone Home Entertainment in home media format. story focuses on former Episcopal priest Graham Hess, played by Mel Gibson, discovers series of crop circles in his cornfield. Hess discovers phenomena are result of extraterrestrial life. stars Joaquin Phoenix, Rory Culkin Abigail Breslin. "Signs" explores faith, kinship, extraterrestrials.
 The Village (2004 film): The Village is a 2004 American psychological horror film, written, produced directed by M. Night Shyamalan starring Joaquin Phoenix, Adrien Brody, Bryce Dallas Howard, William Hurt, Sigourney Weaver, Brendan Gleeson. film is about a village whose inhabitants live in fear of creatures inhabiting woods beyond referred to as "Those We Don't Speak Of." Like other films written directed by Shyamalan from same time period, "The Village" has a twist ending.
The Houses October Built: Houses October Built is a 2014 American found footage horror film and directorial debut of Bobby Roe, also starred in movie produced by Zack Andrews (who also starred) and Steven Schneider, whose hits include "Paranormal Activity", "Insidious", "The Devil Inside" and M. Night Shyamalan's "The Visit" and "Split". film given limited theatrical release on October 10, 2014 released to home video on January 6, 2015. Filming partially took place at several haunted house attractions, Roe would later include in list of "America's Scariest Haunted Houses" released as marketing material for film.

Gerstein Report: Gerstein Report written in 1945 by Kurt Gerstein, Obersturmführer (First Lieutenant) of Waffen-SS rose to Head of Technical Disinfection Services SS supplied hydrogen cyanide (Zyklon B) from Degesch ("Deutsche Gesellschaft für Schädlingsbekämpfung") to Rudolf Höss in Auschwitz conducted negotiations with owners. 17 August 1942 with Rolf Günther Wilhelm Pfannenstiel Gerstein witnessed gassing of 3,000 Jews in extermination camp of Belzec in occupied Poland. report features eyewitness testimony used as evidence in Nuremberg Trials.
 Rudolf Höss: Rudolf Höss (also Höß, Hoeß or Hoess; 25 November 1901 – 16 April 1947) was Nazi German "SS"-"Obersturmbannführer" (lieutenant colonel) longest-serving commandant of Auschwitz concentration and extermination camp in World War II. tested carried effect methods to accelerate Hitler's plan to exterminate Jewish population of Nazi-occupied Europe known as "Final Solution". On initiative of SS-"Hauptsturmführer" (captain) Karl Fritzsch Höss introduced pesticide Zyklon B containing hydrogen cyanide to killing process allowing SS soldiers at Auschwitz to murder 2,000 people every hour created largest installation for continuous annihilation of human beings ever known.
 Jasenovac concentration camp: Jasenovac camp ( Yiddish: יאסענאוואץ ) was extermination camp established in Slavonia by authorities of Independent State of Croatia (NDH) during World War II. camp established by governing Ustaše regime not operated by Nazi Germany. one of largest concentration camps in Europe referred to as "the Auschwitz of the Balkans" and "the Yugoslav Auschwitz".
Auschwitz concentration camp: (German: "Konzentrationslager Auschwitz" also "KZ Auschwitz " or "KL Auschwitz ") was a network of German Nazi concentration camps and extermination camps built operated by Third Reich in Polish areas annexed by Nazi Germany during World War II. consisted of original camp), Auschwitz II–Birkenau combination concentration/extermination camp), (a labor camp staff IG Farben factory), 45 satellite camps.
 Majdanek concentration camp: Majdanek, or KL Lublin, was a German concentration and extermination camp built operated by SS on outskirts of city Lublin during German occupation of Poland in World War II. initially purposed for forced labor, camp used to kill people industrial scale during Operation Reinhard, German plan to murder all Jews within General Government territory of Poland. camp operated from October 1, 1941, until July 22, 1944 captured nearly intact because rapid advance of Soviet Red Army during "Operation Bagration" prevented "SS" from destroying infrastructure Deputy Camp Commandant Anton Thernes failed in removing evidence of war crimes. Majdanek became first concentration camp discovered by Allied forces. Also known as "Konzentrationslager Lublin", Majdanek remains best preserved Nazi concentration camp of the Holocaust.

Treasure Island: Treasure Island is an adventure novel by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson, narrating a tale of "buccaneers and buried gold".
 Long John Silver's: Long John Silver's LLC is an American fast-food restaurant chain specializes in seafood. brand's name is derived from novel "Treasure Island" by Robert Louis Stevenson, in pirate "Long John" Silver is one of main characters. Formerly a division of Yum! Brands, Inc., company was divested to group of franchisees in September 2011.
 Nordsee: Nordsee is a German fast-food restaurant chain specialising in seafood. In addition to selling raw and smoked seafood, company also sells wide variety of meals and products prepared from seafood such as Fischbrötchen (fish sandwiches), salads, and canned seafood. company formerly supplied its own seafood but since sold the fishery.
 Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard: Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard is a Golden, Colorado-based fast-food restaurant specializing in premium burgers and frozen custard. Good Times Restaurants Inc. owns and operates 38 Good Times Burgers & Frozen Custard locations, 36 in Colorado, and two in Wyoming.
 The Crab Cooker: The Crab Cooker is a popular Southern California restaurant specializing in seafood, located on Balboa Peninsula in Newport Beach, California. restaurant housed in old branch building of Bank of America located at 22nd & Newport Blvd. logo of bank prior to merger with NationsBank can still be seen embedded in corner of building. It established in 1951, considered a local landmark. In 1969, Venture Magazine rated it as one of the top two restaurants in world.
 McDonaldization: McDonaldization is a term used by sociologist George Ritzer in his book "The McDonaldization of Society" (1993). explains it becomes manifested when society adopts characteristics of a fast-food restaurant. McDonaldization is a reconceptualization of rationalization and scientific management.Where Max Weber used model of bureaucracy to represent direction of this changing society, Ritzer sees fast-food restaurant as become a more representative contemporary paradigm (Ritzer, 2004:553). The process of McDonaldization can be summarized as way in "the principles of the fast-food restaurant are coming to dominate more and more sectors of American society as well as of the rest of the world."

Forsaken (album): Forsaken is third studio album by Christian black metal band Antestor released 2005 on Endtime Productions. album features guest appearances of established metal musicians Jan Axel Blomberg (Hellhammer) Ann-Mari Edvardsen.
 Mezzerschmitt: Mezzerschmitt is Norwegian black metal band spinoff of Mayhem formed in 2000 by Mayhem members Jan Axel Blomberg (Hellhammer) and Rune Eriksen (Blasphemer), collaborating with Lars Sørensen from Red Harvest. intended to create industrial metal band but sound soon shifted towards black metal while still incorporating industrial elements. Mezzerschmitt released one EP, "Weltherrschaft".
 Steinar Sverd Johnsen: Steinar Sverd Johnsen is Norwegian keyboardist and composer born 1972. Sverd plays keyboards synthesizers in Arcturus main composer for band. formed band with Jan Axel Blomberg (also known as Hellhammer) of Mayhem in 1987 originally under moniker Mortem (where played guitar). band split up in April 2007, reformed in 2011.
 Jan Axel Blomberg: Jan Axel "Hellhammer" Blomberg (born 2 August 1969) Norwegian heavy metal drummer best known as drummer of Mayhem joined in 1988. 1987 Blomberg formed avant-garde black metal band Arcturus (under name Mortem) with Steinar Sverd Johnsen broke up in April 2007 reunited in 2011. named himself after Swiss extreme metal band Hellhammer. Praised as talented musician Blomberg three-time winner of Spellemannprisen award.
 Mark Gaudet: Mark Gaudet (born October 30, 1963) Canadian musician from Moncton, New Brunswick. played in various indie and metal music groups Elevator, Eric's Trip, Purple Knight Funeral Fog. In 1974, age eleven Gaudet formed first band, Purple Knight. In 1991 Gaudet joined Eric's Trip taking place of former drummer, Ed VaughnMark Gaudet joined Moncton black metal band Funeral Fog in 2003. time Funeral Fog he went by stage name Shithammer inspired by Mayhem's drummer, Hellhammer.
